And neither in the time of the Macedonians from Alexander onwards, not even if you include the reign of Augustus, was anything similar to the words of the prophet fulfilled. For when in those days did the Lord, Whom the prophet speaks of as divine, come among men, and many nations know Him, and confess Him to the only God, and take refuge in Him, and be to Him a people?
The Proof of the Gospel, Book 8, Chapter 4

The Lord heard the prayer of the prophets. The Father did not despise our race, which was perishing; he sent from heaven his own Son the Lord as our physician. One of the prophets says, "The Lord whom you seek, comes; and he shall come suddenly." Where will he come? "The Lord shall come to his temple," where you took up stones against him. Another of the prophets, on hearing this, says to him, "In speaking of God's salvation, do you speak softly? In announcing the good tidings of God's coming for salvation, do you speak in secret?" "Go up onto a high mountain, Zion, herald of glad tidings; say to the cities of Judah"—what shall I say?—"Here is your God! Here comes with power the Lord God." Again the Lord himself has said, " 'Behold, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of you,' says the Lord. 'And many nations shall be joined to the Lord.' " The Israelites rejected salvation through me; "I come to gather nations of every language," for, "he came unto his own, and his own received him not." You come, and what do you bestow upon the nations? "I come to gather nations of every language … I will set a sign among them." For from my conflict on the cross I will give to each of my soldiers a royal sign to bear upon his forehead. Still another prophet said, "He inclined the heavens and came down, with dark clouds under his feet." For his coming down from heaven was unknown to humanity.

But who this people is that is comforted through the Apostles and churchmen, not Israel and Jacob and Judah, as Scripture records in other places, but the people of God, the prophet Zechariah testifies, saying: Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Zion: for I will come and dwell in the midst of you, says the Lord. And many nations shall flee to the Lord in that day, and shall be his people, and they shall dwell in the midst of you, and they shall know that the Lord almighty has sent me to you (Zech 2:10, 11). By this testimony it is clearly shown that very many nations are to be turned into the people of God. And these things the Lord says, sent by the Lord whose name is Almighty.

Praise and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for behold, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of you, says the Lord. And many nations shall be joined to the Lord on that day, and they shall be my people, and I will dwell in the midst of you, and you shall know that the Lord of hosts has sent me to you. And the Lord shall possess Judah as his portion in the sanctified land, and he shall yet choose Jerusalem. LXX: Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Zion, for behold, I will come, and I will dwell in the midst of you, says the Lord. And many nations shall flee for refuge to the Lord on that day, and they shall be his people, and they shall dwell in the midst of you, and you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you, and the Lord shall possess Judah as his portion in the holy land, and he shall yet choose Jerusalem. These words too are to be understood as spoken in the person of the Lord: that he exhorts his people, restored from captivity to its former seat, to be glad and rejoice because the Lord himself is coming and will dwell in its midst; and that many nations are to believe in him, of whom it is said: Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession; and that he dwells in its midst, saying to the disciples: Behold, I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the age; and that the Lord possesses Judah as his portion, Judah that confesses and believes in his name, and possesses it nowhere else than in the holy land, which is interpreted as the Church; and that he yet chooses Jerusalem, which he had abandoned to temptation in the persecutions.

But rightly, after the captivity, is the daughter of Zion called forth to joy, of whom it is also said in the psalm: When the Lord turns back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall exult, and Israel shall be glad.

Some of the Jews think that these things were in part fulfilled under Zerubbabel and Joshua, Ezra and Nehemiah, especially since Jerusalem is chosen and Judah is possessed; that is to say, the two tribes which returned from the Babylonian captivity and were called Judah, and not Israel, which lives among the Medes to this day. Others, however, defer them to the future: that then the nations are to believe in him who is sent by the Lord, and Jerusalem is to be chosen; although surely all the nations have already believed in the Lord Savior, and a city that has been utterly destroyed cannot be chosen.

Let all flesh be silent before the face of the Lord, for he has risen up from his holy dwelling. LXX: Let all flesh fear before the face of the Lord, for he has risen from his holy clouds. Since these things are so, and the Lord is going to possess Judah as his portion and to choose Jerusalem, let the whole race of men dread the coming of the Lord, for he has risen up from his holy dwelling. Now the Lord is said to rise, and as it were to awaken from sleep, when he rises up to avenge his people, according to what is written: Arise, why do you sleep, O Lord? Or else, according to the LXX, who said: He has risen from his holy clouds, understand the patriarchs, prophets and apostles, whom the Lord commanded not to rain rain upon Israel. These are the clouds of which it is written: And let the clouds sprinkle justice; for these bodily clouds, into which the denser air is gathered, cannot rain justice. In these clouds and with these clouds the Lord says in the Gospel that he will come. And in Isaiah we read that the Lord came into Egypt on a light cloud. Egypt is taken as the world, into which the Lord is recorded to have descended in the flesh, which, brought forth from a virginal womb, was weighed down by no weight of human seed and of sins. But that all flesh is to be taken not absolutely, of men and of beasts and of birds and of fish, but specifically of men, is shown by that scripture: Hear my prayer; to you all flesh shall come. For it is not all the flesh of irrational living creatures that is to come to the Lord, but that flesh which is to receive the gift of the Holy Spirit, and of which it is said: I will pour out of my spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy.
3: Also in Zechariah: "And the Lord showed me Jesus, that great priest, standing before the face of the angel of the Lord, and the devil was standing at his right hand to oppose him. And Jesus was clothed in filthy garments, and he stood before the face of the angel himself; and he answered them and said to them who were standing before his face, saying, 'Take away his filthy garments from him.' And he said to him, 'Behold, I have taken away your iniquities.' And put upon him a priestly garment, and set a fair miter upon his head." Also Paul to the Philippians: "Who being established in the form of God, thought it not robbery that he was equal with God, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men; and being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, becoming obedient even unto death, even the death of the cross. Wherefore also God exalted him and gave him a name which is above every name, that in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, of things in earth, and of infernal things, and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord in the glory of God the Father."
Treatise XII. Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews, TESTIMONIES AGAINST THE JEWS 12:2.13

[Passages quoted, Zech. iii. 1—6, 9; vi. 9-13.]

In this passage too the prophet-high-priest called Jesus presents, I think, a very clear picture and plain symbol of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, being honoured by bearing His Name, and made the leader of the return of the people from the Babylonian captivity. Since, also, our Saviour Jesus Christ is said by the Prophet Isaiah to have been sent to preach liberty to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to comfort all that mourn, and to give to all that mourn in Zion glory for dust, the ointment of gladness. You have, therefore, her two great High Priests, first the Christ in Moses, and second the Jesus of whom I am speaking, both bearing in themselves the signs of the truth concerning our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.

But Aaron, the "Christ" in Moses' writings, having freed the people from slavery in Egypt, and led them in freedom and with all carefulness in their journey from Egypt, seems to present a picture of the real Lord, Who has redeemed us, who are of all nations, from Egyptian idolatry; while the Jesus in the prophet, the High Priest who was at the head of the return from Babylon to Jerusalem, also presents a figure of Jesus our Saviour, Whom we have as a great High Priest, that has passed through the heavens, through Whom also we ourselves, redeemed as it were in this present life from Babylon, that is from confusion and slavery, are taught to hasten to the heavenly city, the true Jerusalem.

Jesus too, since he bore in himself the image of the true, was naturally clad in filthy garments, and the devil is said to stand at his right hand and to oppose him, since also Jesus, truly our Saviour and Lord, descending into our state of slavery took away our sins, and washed away the stains of humanity, and underwent the shame of the Passion, through His love for us. Wherefore, Isaiah says:

"He bears our sins, and is pained for us, and we thought him to be in labour, and smitten, and afflicted: He was wounded for our sins, and weakened for our iniquities."

And John the Baptist also, seeing the Lord, said: "Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sins, of the world." Paul also, writing in the same way about Him, says: "Him that knew no sin made sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him," and "Christ has ransomed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us." All these things the inspired prophet referred to when he said, "And Jesus was clad in filthy garments." But He put them from Him by His Ascension into the heavens, and the return from our condition of slavery to His own glory, and He is crowned with the diadem of His Father's Divinity, and is girt with the bright robe of His Father's light, and is glorified with the divine Mitre, and the other high priestly adornments. Nor is it difficult to explain the part about the devil, who even now is opposed to the teaching of Christ, and to His Church established throughout the whole world, and has ever been opposed to our Saviour, and marched against Him before, when He came to save us from our slavery to himself. He tempted Him also the first time, and the second time again, when by the Passion he arranged a plot against Him.
The Proof of the Gospel, Book 4, Chapter 17

For in that passage too, in giving the name of High Priest to Him Who made with His own Blood the priestly propitiation for our sins, he does not by the word "made" declare the first existence of the Only-begotten, but says "made" with the intention of representing that grace which is commonly spoken of in connection with the appointment of priests. For Jesus, the great High Priest (as Zechariah says), Who offered up his own lamb, that is, His own Body, for the sin of the world; Who, by reason of the children that are partakers of flesh and blood, Himself also in like manner took part with them in blood (not in that He was in the beginning, being the Word and God, and being in the form of God, and equal with God, but in that He emptied Himself in the form of the servant, and offered an oblation and sacrifice for us), He, I say, became a High Priest many generations later, after the order of Melchisedech. Surely a reader who has more than a casual acquaintance with the discourse to the Hebrews knows the mystery of this matter.

But because he forgot the commandment of God and fulfilled the will of the serpent, the devil held his hand and caused him to reach for the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, in order to eat of the forbidden fruit. In him, judgment was pronounced on all, and the adversary began to stand at the right hand of all. Hence, that cursed form came forth against Judas: And let the Devil stand at his right hand (Psalm 108:6). If that curse is severe, then this blessing is the greatest, by which the chains of harsh curses are loosened. Therefore, the Lord Jesus placed the devil at His right hand, just as we read in the book of Zechariah (Zach. III, 1); for He had taken up the cause and place of mankind.
THE PRAYER OF JOB AND DAVID 3:10.27

But to sinners the devil stands at the right hand. Yet that discussion is another matter. Whoever is a sinner, the devil stands at his right hand. But someone says: How is it that in Zechariah it is said to stand also to Jesus the son of Josedech? "And the devil was standing at his right hand." How is it written in Zechariah that the devil stands at the right hand of the Savior? You see that there is a question here. But at that time when the devil was standing at the right hand of the Savior, "Jesus," it says, "had filthy garments." He was bearing our sins, he was wrapped in our vices: therefore the devil was standing at his right hand.

It is written in Zechariah: "And he showed me Jesus the great priest standing before the angel of the Lord, and Satan stood at his right hand, to fight with him." If, then, the devil stands at the right hand of the Lord, how does he now say of Judas, And let the devil stand at his right hand? But see what he says. The devil stood at the right hand of Jesus to oppose him: that is, he wished to be an adversary to his right hand. But here he does not say that he wishes to fight, but that he had already conquered Judas. There the devil desires to fight against the right hand; but here he has gained mastery over the right hand of Judas. But this too must be considered. At that time he stood at the Lord's right hand to oppose him, when Jesus had filthy garments. For so it is written there as well: "And Jesus had filthy garments." As long as the Lord Jesus has filthy garments, so long does the devil stand at his right hand: as long as he bears our sins, in our sins the devil opposes him. But when it is said in Zechariah, "Take away his filthy garments and clothe him with the changes of raiment," immediately Jesus says to the devil, "The Lord rebuke you, Satan, may he rebuke you who has chosen Jerusalem."

But perhaps an inquisitive reader will object this too: how we can assert that God stands at the right of the just man, and the devil at the left of the sinner, when concerning our Lord it is read in Zechariah, "And the devil was standing at his right hand to oppose him." Let him, then, who objects this read also what follows: that when the devil was standing at his right hand, Jesus had filthy garments. Rightly did he who had taken up our sins and was bearing our offenses have the devil at his right hand, not so much for himself as for the filthy garments. And at the same time let him consider that it is not said, "The devil was standing as victor and triumphing," but as still set in the contest and in the battle-line and in doubt—indeed, when he had not yet begun to fight. For it follows, "That he might oppose him." But the devil was opposing him, as we said, because he had filthy garments from our sins. But after he heard, "May the Lord who chose Jerusalem rebuke you," he did not stand at the right, but went behind his back and under his feet, and at once Jesus the great priest receives the ankle-length robe (poderis), and is clothed in white vesture, and, royal dignity being joined to him—that is, Zerubbabel being coupled with him—builds the Church, and constructs the spiritual Jerusalem.

And he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord. And Satan was standing at his right hand, to oppose him. And the Lord said to Satan: The Lord rebuke you, Satan, and the Lord rebuke you, he who has chosen Jerusalem. Is not this a brand plucked out of the fire? And Joshua was clothed in filthy garments, and was standing before the face of the angel, who answered and said to those who were standing before him, saying: Take away the filthy garments from him. And he said to him: Behold, I have taken away your iniquity from you, and I have clothed you with changes of raiment. And he said: Put a clean tiara upon his head; and they put a clean tiara upon his head, and they clothed him with garments. LXX: And the Lord showed me Joshua the high priest, standing before the face of the angel of the Lord, and the devil was standing at his right hand, to oppose him. And the Lord said to the devil: The Lord rebuke you, devil, and the Lord who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you. Is not this like a brand plucked out of the fire? And Joshua was clothed in filthy garments, and was standing before the face of the angel, and he answered and said to those standing before his face, saying: Take away the filthy garments from him. And he said to him: Behold, I have taken away your iniquities from you; and clothe him with a robe reaching to the feet, and set a clean tiara upon his head; and they set a clean tiara upon his head, and they put garments about him. Before we come to the spiritual understanding, we must say succinctly and briefly how the Hebrews explain this passage. Joshua (Iesus, the same name as Jesus) the high priest, whom the Greeks call ἀρχιερέα, the Latins pontiff, they take to be the son of Jehozadak, who presided over the people together with Zerubbabel. At his right hand the adversary was standing (for this is what satan means), to oppose him. And rightly was he standing at his right hand, not at his left, because the accusation was true, since he too, along with the rest, had taken a foreign wife, as is written most fully in Ezra and in Malachi, who follows this prophet.

Our writers, however, explain it thus: that he is the high priest to whom it is said: You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek. Since he cannot be seen of himself, he is shown to the prophet by the Lord, standing before the angel of the Lord, whom they take to be the angel of great counsel: not that he is one and another, so that we should admit two persons in the Son, but that he is one and the same, and is both shown as a man in soiled clothing and said to appear as an angel, the mediator of men and God. And that he is not Joshua son of Jehozadak they try to show from this, that the words son of Jehozadak are not added in the present place, whereas in other places, where it is truly Joshua son of Jehozadak who is spoken of, he is always registered by his father's name. So Jesus is seen standing, set firm with a steady step: And Satan standing at his right hand, to oppose him. For he was tempted in every way, without sin. And in the Gospel the tempter approaches him, seeking always to oppose his right-hand works and his virtues.

I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not.  And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.  Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.  Likewise also these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities.  Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee. [Zechariah 3:2] But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves.  Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.  These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots;  Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever.

[Passage quoted, Zech. iii. 1.]

AND here again the Lord says that another Lord will rebuke the devil. The Lord that is speaking with Him is not himself the rebuker, but tells of another Lord. Wherein I consider there is clear proof of the existence of two Lords, the Father and God of the Universe, and One after the Father, Who has received the lordship and dominion of all things begotten.
The Proof of the Gospel, Book 5, Chapter 27

You can search them out for yourself from sacred Scripture without my help. And it will become clearly evident to you that this likely is the age of which it was said, "Believe not in friends and trust not in princes," and that the prophecy is now being fulfilled: "The leaders of my people have not known me; they are foolish and senseless children. They are wise to do evils, but to do good they have no knowledge." We should rather pity such people than hate them and should rather pray for them than revile them. For we were created to bless and not to revile. Thus also Michael, when he was arguing with the devil over the body of Moses, did not dare to bring an accusation of blasphemy against him even for such a serious offense but said, "May the Lord rebuke you." Even in Zechariah, we read something similar to this. "The Lord rebuke you, O Satan, and the Lord that chose Jerusalem rebuke you." And so we also pray that those who refuse to be rebuked by their friends with humility may be rebuked by the Lord.

And the Lord said to Satan, to the accuser and his adversary, for he is the enemy and avenger, the accuser of his brothers: The Lord rebuke you, Satan, as the Lord rained from the Lord, and the Lord rebuke you, he who has chosen Jerusalem. Since, then, out of all the cities of Judah Jerusalem has now been chosen, the Lord in no way imputing to her the sins she committed, why do you try to overwhelm Joshua like a brand, which is commonly called a firebrand, Joshua who escaped as it were half-burnt from the Babylonian captivity?

As for what follows: The Lord rebuke you, Satan, and the Lord rebuke you, he who has chosen Jerusalem, they explain it thus: that the Father and the Son is Lord, and in Psalm 109 (110) we read: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand; he speaks of the other Lord, not because the Lord himself who speaks cannot rebuke, but because, from the unity of their nature, when the other has rebuked, he himself who speaks rebukes: For he who sees the Son sees the Father, and he it is who has chosen Jerusalem, the Church, which contemplates the peace of the Lord. Now the brand plucked out of the fire can most rightly be understood as him who, though he was in Babylon, was not consumed by the Babylonian fire, nor touched by the flame of this world. Hence Moses too, in the wilderness, sees a great vision, in which the bush was burning and was not consumed.

This is also a type of our situation. Just as the avenging and wicked devil was very opposed to Joshua for being high priest and making intercession to God on behalf of the people, so in turn this same enemy was an opponent of Jesus the great high priest in the order of Melchizedek for taking away the sin of the world15 and wished to bring him down. It was, however, not Joshua the son of Jehozadak that rebuked him, but Joshua's Lord; when he approached Jesus the Savior of the world, he was rebuked by him, as by his God and Lord, and hears, "Get behind me, Satan."

"But to give you the account of the revelation of the holy Jesus Christ, I take up again my discourse, and I assert that even that revelation was made for us who believe on Christ the High Priest, namely this crucified One; and though we lived in fornication and all kinds of filthy conversation, we have by the grace of our Jesus, according to His Father's will, stripped ourselves of all those filthy wickednesses with which we were imbued. And though the devil is ever at hand to resist us, and anxious to seduce all to himself, yet the Angel of God, i.e., the Power of God sent to us through Jesus Christ, rebukes him, and he departs from us. And we are just as if drawn out from the fire, when purified from our former sins, and [rescued] from the affliction and the fiery trial by which the devil and all his coadjutors try us; out of which Jesus the Son of God has promised again to deliver us, and invest us with prepared garments, if we do His commandments; and has undertaken to provide an eternal kingdom [for us]. For just as that Jesus (Joshua), called by the prophet a priest, evidently had on filthy garments because he is said to have taken a harlot for a wife, and is called a brand plucked out of the fire, because he had received remission of sins when the devil that resisted him was rebuked; even so we, who through the name of Jesus have believed as one man in God the Maker of all, have been stripped, through the name of His first-begotten Son, of the filthy garments, i.e., of our sins; and being vehemently inflamed by the word of His calling, we are the true high priestly race of God, as even God Himself bears witness, saying that in every place among the Gentiles sacrifices are presented to Him well-pleasing and pure. Now God receives sacrifices from no one, except through His priests."

Every soul that has been clothed with a human body has its own "filth". And that you may know that Jesus too was made filthy by his own will, because for our salvation he had assumed a human body, listen to the prophet Zechariah saying: "Jesus was clothed with filthy garments". And this indeed makes against those who deny that our Lord had a human body, but say it was woven of heavenly and spiritual things. For if his body was of heavenly things and, as they falsely assert, of the stars and some other more sublime and spiritual nature, let them answer why a spiritual body could be filthy, or how they interpret what we have set down: "Jesus was clothed with filthy garments". But if they are compelled by necessity to accept that a filthy garment is understood as a spiritual body, they must consequently say that what is set down in the promises has been fulfilled, that is: "an animal body is sown, a spiritual body rises," and that we rise polluted and filthy — which even to think is a sacrilege, especially when one knows it is written: "it is sown in corruption, it will rise in incorruption; it is sown in dishonor, it will rise in glory; it is sown in weakness, it will rise in strength; an animal body is sown, a spiritual body will rise". It was necessary, therefore, that for our Lord and Savior, who had been "clothed with filthy garments" and had assumed an earthly body, there should be offered those things which by the law were accustomed to purge filth. What is frequently asked among the brethren I take up again, prompted by the occasion of this passage. Little children are baptized "for the remission of sins". Of what "sins"? Or at what time did they sin? Or how can that reasoning of the washing hold in the case of little children, except according to that sense of which we spoke a little before: "no one is clean from filth, not even if his life should be of a single day upon the earth"? And because through the sacrament of baptism the "filth" of birth is laid aside, therefore little children too are baptized: for "unless one be born again of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of heaven".
HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 14

Now who this one would be to whom God promised an eternal priesthood Zechariah has taught, even giving his name most clearly. For thus he spoke: "And the Lord God showed me Jesus the high priest standing before the face of the angel of the Lord, and the devil stood at his right hand to be his adversary. And the Lord said to the devil, 'May the Lord that chose Jerusalem rule over you, and behold the brand plucked out of the fire!' And Jesus was clothed with filthy garments, and he stood before the face of the angel. And he answered and said to them that stood around before his face, saying, 'Take away the filthy garments from him, and put on him a tunic and sandals, and put a clean miter upon his head.' And they clothed him with garments and put a clean miter upon his head. And the angel of the Lord stood and testified before Jesus, saying, 'Thus says the Lord almighty: If you will walk in my ways and keep my charges, you shall judge my house. And I will give you some of them that are now present to walk with you.' Hear, then, O Jesus, the high priest."

Now in this, by that wondrous sacrifice, Elijah clearly proclaimed to us the sacramental rite of baptism that should afterwards be instituted. For the fire was kindled by water thrice poured upon it, so that it is clearly shown that where the mystic water is, there is the kindling, warm and fiery spirit that burns up the ungodly and illuminates the faithful. Yes, and yet again his disciple Elisha, when Naaman the Syrian, who was diseased with leprosy, had come to him as a suppliant, cleanses the sick man by washing him in the Jordan, clearly indicating what should come, both by the use of water generally and by dipping in the river in particular. For the Jordan alone of rivers, receiving in itself the firstfruits of sanctification and benediction, conveyed in its channel to the whole world, as it were from some fount in the type afforded by itself, the grace of baptism. These then are indications in deed and act of regeneration in baptism. Let us for the rest consider the prophecies of it in words and language. Isaiah cried, saying, "Wash you, make you clean, put away evil from your souls," and David, "Draw nigh to him and be enlightened, and your faces shall not be ashamed." And Ezekiel, writing more clearly and plainly than them both, says, "And I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be cleansed; from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I give you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh, and my spirit will I put within you." Most manifestly also does Zechariah prophesy of Joshua, who was clothed with filthy garments (to wit, the flesh of a servant, even ours), and stripping him of his ill-favored raiment, adorns him with the clean and fair apparel, teaching us by the figurative illustration that truly in the baptism of Jesus all we, putting off our sins like some poor and patched garment, are clothed in the holy and most fair garment of regeneration.

As for what follows: Joshua was clothed in filthy garments, they interpret it in three ways: either on account of the unlawful marriage, or on account of the sins of the people, or because of the squalor of the captivity. Now the angel before whose face Joshua was standing commanded the other angels, in the person of the Lord, to take away from him the filthy garments of which we spoke above. When they had fulfilled the command in deed, the same angel speaks again to Joshua: Behold, I have taken away your iniquity from you; these are the filthy garments; and I have clothed you with changes of raiment; that is, I have joined an Israelite wife to you; for which the Seventy translated ποδήρη, which we can call an ankle-length tunic, because it flows down to the ankles and feet.

This Jesus was clothed in filthy garments, who, though he had committed no sin, was made sin for us. And he bears our infirmities, and grieves for us, and we reckoned him to be in sorrow, and under a blow, and in anguish. But he was wounded for our iniquities, and was made weak for our sins. And in the apostle Paul we read: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us. It is he who speaks in Psalm 21 (22): Far from my salvation are the words of my offences. And in Psalm 68 (69): O God, you know my foolishness, and my offences are not hidden from you. All these are called filthy garments, and they will be taken away from him when he has blotted out our sins, so that, because he was clothed in filthy garments, we, rising again, may hear in him after baptism: Let your garments be always white; and the whole Church of believers hears through Isaiah: Wash yourselves, be clean. And of her it is prophesied in the Song of Songs: Who is this who comes up made white? Ποδήρην, moreover, take to be his incarnation, which is from the earth and is signified in the feet. By the clean tiara upon his head understand the splendor of the divine majesty, so that one and the same may be seen to be adorned, according to the man, with the ποδήρη, and according to God, with the tiara.

Holy Job says, when speaking about his own sins, "for man that is born of a woman is short-lived and full of wrath: as the flower of grass, so does he fall; and he departs like a shadow, nor shall he stay. Hast Thou not taken account even of him, and caused him to enter into judgment in Thy sight? For who shall be pure from uncleanness? Not even one, even if his life should be but of one day upon the earth." Now when he speaks of uncleanness here, the mere perusal of the passage is enough to show that he meant sin to be understood. It is plain from the words, of what he is speaking. The same phrase and sense occur in the prophet Zechariah, in the place where "the filthy garments" are removed from off the high priest, and it is said to him, "I have taken away thy sins." Well now, I rather think that all these passages, and others of like import, which point to the fact that man is born in sin and under the curse, are not to be read among the dark recesses of the Manicheans, but in the sunshine of catholic truth.

And as for what follows: Put a clean tiara upon his head, for tiara we read in the Hebrew Saniph, which most people call a mitre; and by this they want the dignity of the priesthood to be understood, because, once the filth of his sins had been taken away, he held a clean priesthood. This is what the Jews say.

And the angel of the Lord was standing.

And the angel of the Lord solemnly charged Joshua, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: If you walk in my ways and keep my charge, you also shall judge my house, and shall keep my courts, and I will give you those who walk, from among these who now stand by here. LXX: And the angel of the Lord was standing. And the angel of the Lord solemnly charged Joshua, saying: Thus says the Lord Almighty: If you walk in my ways and keep my precepts, you too shall judge my house; and if you keep my court, I will give you those who shall move about in the midst of these who stand here. The Hebrews, following the course of the interpretation they have begun, understand these things to have been said by the angel of the Lord to Joshua (Iesus, the same name as Jesus) son of Jehozadak: that after the removal of the filthy garments and the restoration of the dignity of a clean priesthood, he is given a command according to what is written in the Gospel: Behold, you have been made well; sin no more, lest something worse befall you; and a reward is promised him, if he walks in the ways of the Lord and keeps his precepts: that he himself should be the judge of his house, that is, should continue as high priest in the temple, and should keep his courts and porches; and that the Lord should give him some from the number of the angels who at that time stood in his sight, so that he might be walled about by their help and be secure from every treachery of his enemies. According to our writers, who refer all these things to the Lord Savior, this seems to be difficult: that it is said to Jesus by the angel that if he walks in the ways of the Lord and keeps his precepts, he too shall judge his house and keep his courts, and the Lord shall give him those who walk, from among those who stand by him. This is easily resolved if we consider him who deigned to take the form of a servant. And though he was rich, he became poor for us. Whatever, then, is said of the members is referred to the body; our progress is the Lord's victory. And when we have come to the perfect man, to the measure of the age of the fullness of Christ, he will judge the house of God, according to what the Apostle said: But Christ as a son over his house, whose house we are, and to Timothy: If I delay, that you may know how you ought to conduct yourself in the house of God, which is the Church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth. And not only will he judge his house, but he will also keep the courts of the Lord, of which it is written: Worship the Lord in his holy court. And he will judge, or discern, his house, and according to the merits of each, giving to one ten cities and to another five, and appointing some in the Church as prophets, some as apostles, some as teachers, some as workers of signs, holding some as eyes, some as hands, some as feet, according to what we read: God has stood in the assembly of the gods, and in the midst he discerns the gods. He also gave him ministers from the number of the angels, who, though set in the flesh, are like the angels, and of whom the Apostle spoke: Our citizenship is in the heavens. For if the angels neither marry nor are given in marriage, and those who persevere in virginal continence are like the angels, why should we not think that the apostles and all the saints, being of angelic dignity, were given to Jesus, to stand by him in the Church and never to have wavering feet, but to stand with the Lord who stands?

But in all battles He triumphed over the devil, and all the unseen enemies and foes led by him, and made us who were slaves His own people, and built of us, as of living stones, the house of God, and the state of holiness, so that He exactly agrees with the oracle, which says:

"Behold a man, whose name is the Branch. And he shall spring up from below, and shall build the house of the Lord. And he shall receive virtue, and shall sit and rule upon his throne."

Note, therefore, with care, in what manner in speaking mystically of the Jesus of days of old, who bears the image of the true, he says: "Behold a man, whose name is the Branch." And a little later, it is said to Jesus himself then present, as if concerning some one else who was the Branch: "Hear, Jesus, the High Priest, thou and thy neighbour, for the men are diviners. Behold, I bring my servant the Branch."

If, then, the speech related to some one yet to come, who was more truly called the Branch than he that bore the name then, he must have been only an image of him that was yet to come, as he is not only called Jesus in figure, but the Branch as well, if this was said to him when present: "Behold a man, whose name is the Branch." He was, therefore, naturally because he was the image thought worthy of the name of the Saviour, as well as of the Branch: for the name of Jesus translated into Greek means "Salvation of God." For in Hebrew "Isoua" is "salvation," and the son of Nave is called by the Hebrews Joshua, Joshua being "Salvation of Jab," that is, Salvation of God. It follows that wherever the Salvation of God is named in the Greek versions, you are to understand that nothing but Jesus is meant.
The Proof of the Gospel, Book 4, Chapter 17

Of Him He has also spoken by the mouth of the prophet Ezekiel, saying, "I will set up one Shepherd over them, and He shall feed them, even My Servant David, He shall feed them, and He shall be their Shepherd. And I the Lord will be their God, and My Servant David a Prince among them." Now king David was already dead, and therefore the true David, the truly humble, the truly meek, the true Son of God, strong of hand, is announced by this name; he also is intended in the book of the prophet Zechariah, where God the Father says, "Behold I will send my servant, the Orient is His name." Did then His being "clothed in filthy garments" deprive the Sun of righteousness of the brightness of His Godhead?

Hear, O Joshua, high priest, you and your friends who dwell before you, for they are men who portend. For behold, I will bring my servant the Rising, for behold the stone which I have given before Joshua: upon one stone are seven eyes. LXX: Hear then, O Joshua, high priest, and your neighbours who sit before your face, for the men τερατοσκόποι, that is, of portents, are beholders, for behold, I will bring my servant the Rising, for the stone which I have given before the face of Joshua, upon one stone are seven eyes. Our writers are hard pressed in this place by the Jews, on the ground that, following the sequence and texture of the discourse, they ought rather to understand Joshua (Iesus, the same name as Jesus) the priest, son of Jehozadak, than the Lord Savior. For if the word is addressed to the Lord, and to Christ it is said: Hear, O Joshua, high priest, who is the one of whom it is added: Behold, I will bring my servant the Rising, who by another name is called the stone, and has been given before Joshua, and upon this stone are seven eyes? Our writers, on the contrary, strive to maintain that Christ is called, according to different understandings, both Jesus the high priest, and the Rising, and the stone. But how they could explain that this is said of him, to him, as though of another, is most difficult. Those, then, who want the high priest to be Joshua son of Jehozadak interpret his friends who dwell, or sit, before him, and who are men who portend, as his disciples and the prophets. For the prophets were set as a sign of things to come. What is it, then, that Joshua and his friends are made to hear: I will bring my servant the Rising, and the rest? Because above God had promised Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, that if he walked in his ways and kept his precepts, he himself would judge his house and keep his courts, and that he would give him ministers of angelic dignity, now he tells him and his friends that full happiness and perfect blessedness will come then, when the Rising comes, of whom it is written: Behold a man, the Rising is his name. And in Malachi: For you who fear my name the sun of justice shall rise, and healing in its wings. And in Numbers: A star shall rise out of Jacob, and a man out of Israel. In the Gospel too we read most plainly of Christ: In which the Rising from on high will visit us. To give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace. He himself is called the Rising and the cornerstone, because he joins both peoples together and unites two walls into one house. To those who do not believe he is a stone of stumbling, of whom it is also said in the psalms: The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner. This was done by the Lord. Upon this stone are seven eyes, of which Isaiah speaks: A rod shall come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up from his root, and the spirit of God shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and fortitude, the spirit of knowledge and piety; and the spirit of the fear of God shall fill him.

Those who want the high priest and his friends to be understood as the Lord Savior and his disciples take the men τερατοσκόπους, men who portend, in this way: they refer them to the apostles, who perceived his mystical signs and recognized the future from the present; while in the man who was blind from birth they interpret the restored eyes as concerning the people of the Gentiles, and in the woman with the flow of blood they explain the Church as set free from the works of blood.

And definitely did He show concerning this stone:—Lo! on this stone will I open seven eyes. And what then are the seven eyes that were opened on the stone? Clearly the Spirit of God that abode on Christ with seven operations, as Isaiah the Prophet said:—The Spirit of God shall rest and dwell upon Him, (a spirit) of wisdom and understanding, of counsel and of courage, of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord. These were the seven eyes that were opened upon the Stone, and these are the seven eyes of the Lord which look upon all the earth.

As for what is written according to the Seventy: Behold, I will dig a pit, we can understand the ditch or pit in place of the carving of the stone: for everything that is carved is also dug. Yet if someone, more contentiously, will not refer this to the stone, but would have it hold, as it were, its own beginning and its own meaning, let us say that the Lord Almighty, on the day of his Son's passion, or else — as the Jews think, at the final end of the world, when he comes to judge — digs out and brings into the open the works of each person, and handles the whole earth on the day of judgment; for this is the one day, and on that day each of the saints calls his companions and friends, who are themselves also saints, to rest, and rejoices in the virtue of his works.

As for what follows: For behold the stone which I have given before Joshua, the lovers of the history understand it of Christ in this way, saying that Christ was to come after Joshua son of Jehozadak. For this, they say, is what before Joshua means, that is, in his sight and before his face, so that it signifies things to come; and he is called a stone for his strength and hardness, with which he crushed all kingdoms, the stone which we also read in Daniel was cut from the mountain without hands.

Behold, I will engrave its carving, says the Lord of hosts, and I will take away the iniquity of that land in one day.

On that day, says the Lord of hosts, a man shall call his friend under the vineyard and under the fig tree. LXX: Behold, I will dig a pit, says the Lord Almighty, and I will handle all the iniquity of that land in one day. On that day, says the Lord Almighty, each one shall call his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree. Above he had said: Behold the stone which I have given before Joshua, upon one stone are seven eyes. Now, consistently, he keeps the μεταφορὰν (metaphor) taken from the stone, and says: I will engrave its carving, or I will carve its engraving. For where it is written in Hebrew maphate phethee, Aquila translated διαγλύψω ἄνοιγμα αὐτῆς, that is, I will carve its opening; Theodotion and Symmachus, I will carve its carving. And the sense is: I will cause this stone to be wounded by the nails of the cross and the soldier's lance, and in his passion I will take away the iniquity of the land in one day, the day of which it is written: This is the day which the Lord has made; let us exult and rejoice in it.

These are the "seven eyes" of the Lamb, and the "seven facets" of the stone mentioned by Zachary, and the seven days that followed upon the first light. These Centers are the "seven golden lamp-stands," and Christ "in the midst of the seven lamp-stands," which are the seven illuminations of wisdom, that is, the metaphysical, the natural, the mathematical, the logical, the ethical, the political, and the theological.

On that day of the passion of Christ, the man who is perfect in Christ, and who with the apostles ascends to the summit of the Lord's goodwill, shall call his neighbour, either the believers from among the Jews or at any rate the people of the Gentiles, under the vineyard which is called Sorek, and of which he says in the Gospel: I am the vine, and whose fruit gladdens the heart of man; and under the fig tree, the sweetest fruits of the Holy Spirit, so that they may rest in eternal peace and, the sedition of the world and the gore of warriors having been suppressed, may know that they are under a king whose name, mystically in Solomon, is that of peace. Of this same sitting under the vineyard and under the fig tree the prophet Micah also makes mention, saying: On that day each one shall call his neighbour and his brother under the fig tree and his vineyard, and there shall be none to terrify them.
4: And the angel who was speaking in me returned, and roused me like a man who is roused from his sleep. LXX: And the angel who was speaking in me returned, and roused me as a man is wont to be roused from his sleep. For where had he gone, that he should return, especially he who was speaking in the prophet, and who could not be apart from him in whom he was speaking? But whenever human frailty is left to its own weakness, we must believe that God, and the help of his angels, departs from us. So the prophet too, stunned with amazement at the great vision, was numb in his whole mind and could not see the clear light of truth; hence he is roused from the past vision to another vision, as though waking from sleep, so that he may see what with closed eyes he did not see. Let us also say it another way. There is a testimony in the Proverbs of Solomon: If you sit down, you will be without fear; but if you sleep, you will sleep sweetly, and you will not fear the terror coming upon you, nor the onslaughts of the ungodly bearing down on you. Whoever sleeps this sleep, and hears said of himself what we read written of Lazarus: If he sleeps, he will be well, will be able to sing with the bride: I sleep, and my heart keeps watch. Let us see, then, for the contemplation of what things the prophet rises as if from sleep.

Behold the seven horns of the Lamb, the seven eyes of God -the seven eyes are the seven spirits of the Lamb; seven torches burning before the throne of God seven golden candlesticks, seven young sheep, the seven women in Isaiah, the seven churches in Paul, seven deacons, seven angels, seven trumpets, seven seals to the book, seven periods of seven days with which Pentecost is completed, the seven weeks in Daniel, also the forty-three weeks in Daniel; with Noah, seven of all clean things in the ark; seven revenges of Cain, seven years for a debt to be acquitted, the lamp with seven orifices, seven pillars of wisdom in the house of Solomon.
On the Creation of the World

Now let us discuss what has been written by churchmen in their commentaries. They understand the golden lampstand of purest gold as the Church, which in the holy Scriptures searches out the sense and the mind rather than the words. And that gold is taken to mean the sense is shown by the back and shoulders of the dove in Psalm 67 (68), which are said to shine with the green or the gleam of gold. The lamp they too understand as Christ himself, because he shines in the Church, he who said of himself: No one lights a lamp and puts it under a bushel, that is, under the measure of the law, but upon a lampstand, that is, the freedom of the Gospel, so that it may give light to all who are in the house. The seven lamps and their pourers they too understand as the graces of the Holy Spirit, through which the Church receives the oil of the mercy of God and of all the virtues. The two olive trees upon the lampstand they too understand as Moses and Elijah, who were talking with the Lord on the mountain and signifying what he was to suffer in Jerusalem. For the whole law and the prophets proclaim the passion of Christ. Others interpret the two olive trees on the right and on the left as the law and the Gospel, so that the Gospel is on the right and the law on the left; of which right and left it is said in the Song of Songs: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.

And he said to me: What do you see? And I said: I have seen, and behold, a lampstand all of gold, and its lamp upon its head; and its seven lamps upon it, seven and seven pourers for the lamps which were upon its head. And two olive trees upon it, one on the right of the lamp, and one on its left. And I answered, and I say to the angel who was speaking in me, saying: What are these, my lord? And the angel who was speaking in me answered, and said to me: Do you not know what these are? And I said: No, my lord. And he answered, and said to me, saying: This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel, saying: Not by an army, nor by strength, but by my spirit, says the Lord of hosts. Who are you, O great mountain, before Zerubbabel? Into a plain! And he shall bring out the chief stone, and shall make equal the grace of its grace. LXX: And he said to me: What do you see? And I said: I have seen, and behold, a lampstand all of gold, and a lamp upon it; and seven lamps upon it, and seven pourers of the lamps which were upon it. And behold, two olive trees upon it, one on the right of the lamp, and one on the left; and I asked, and said to the angel who was speaking in me, saying: What are these, lord? And the angel who was speaking in me answered and said to me: Do you not know what these are? And I said: No, lord. And he answered and said to me, saying: This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel, saying: Not by great might, nor by strength, but by my spirit, says the Lord Almighty. Who are you, O great mountain, before the face of Zerubbabel, that you should set right? And I will bring out the stone of inheritance, the equality of grace, its grace. The angel who roused Zechariah, like a man rising from sleep, asks him what he has seen, so that, when he answers and does not know, and inquires what it is that he sees, and says: What are these, my lord?, we may hear from him: This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel: Not by an army, nor by strength, but by my spirit, says the Lord. Let us therefore go through the details one by one and say first what the Hebrews think, by whom we have been taught in the Old Testament; then by these, as by steps, let us climb to the heights of the Church. The lampstand of solid gold they interpret as the law, that is, νόμον. The lamp, that is, the flame shining and gleaming on the top of the lampstand, they take as Christ, who is the head of the law and gives light to the whole world. The seven lamps upon the lampstand they take as the seven graces of the Holy Spirit, of which we spoke above, saying that on one stone there are seven eyes. For no one doubts that the law was written at the dictation of the Holy Spirit. And by the seven pourers, in which is the oil that is sent into the lamps that shine upon the lampstand, they would have it understood that these seven graces come down from heaven to men through the law. And the two olive trees upon the lampstand, on the right side and on the left, between which the lamp shines in the middle, they interpret as the law and prophecy. And when the prophet had told his vision, not knowing what he was seeing, he asks the angel who was speaking in him, that is, his mind enlightened by God. For this is our angel, who, understanding wisely, shows us the will of God, and he says: What are these, my lord? But the angel does not explain the vision to the prophet, as he had been asked by him, but questions in turn the one who questions him: Do you not know what these are? And when he answers, I do not know, he himself also answers: This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel, saying: Not by an army, nor by strength; but by my spirit, says the Lord. The word of the Lord to Zerubbabel, then, which spoke not by an army, nor by strength, but by my spirit, is itself the interpretation of the vision: that not by an army nor by a multitude of warriors, but by the spirit of God, the people had been brought back and would be brought back more fully, and the adversaries would be laid waste.

Zechariah shows that the olive shadows forth the law of Moses, speaking thus: "And the angel that talked with me came again, and waked me, as a man that is wakened out of his sleep, and said to me, 'What do you see?' And I said, 'I have looked, and behold a candlestick all of gold, with a bowl on the top of it, … and two olive trees by it, one on the right side of the bowl and the other on its left side.' " And after a few words, the prophet, asking what are the olives on the right and the left of the candlestick and what are the two olive boughs in the hands of the two pipes, the angel answered and said, "These are the two sons of fruitfulness which stand by the Lord of the whole earth." [These signify] the two firstborn virtues that are waiting upon God, which, in his dwelling, supply around the wick, through the boughs, the spiritual oil of God, that humanity may have the light of divine knowledge. But the two boughs of the two olives are the law and the prophets, around, as it were, the lot of the inheritance, of which Christ and the Holy Spirit are the authors. We ourselves, meanwhile, [are] not being able to take the whole fruit and the greatness of these plants, before chastity began to rule the world, but only their boughs—namely, the law and the prophets—did we formerly cultivate, and those moderately, often letting them slip. For who was ever able to receive Christ or the Spirit, unless he first purified himself? For the exercise which prepares the soul from childhood for desirable and delectable glory, and carries this grace safely there with ease, and from small toils raises up mighty hopes, is chastity, which gives immortality to our bodies. It becomes all people willingly to prefer in honor and to praise above all things; some, that by its means they may be betrothed to the word, practicing virginity; and others, that by it they may be freed from the curse, "Dust you are, and to dust you will return." This, O Arete, is the discourse on virginity which you required of me, accomplished according to my ability; which I pray, O mistress, although it is mediocre and short, that you will receive with kindness from me who was chosen to speak last.

However, since here in Genesis we read that paradise was planted by God in the East, and there the man whom God formed was placed; we can now find the author of this paradise. For who else could have created paradise but the all-powerful God, who spoke and things came into being, never needing those things which he desired to be generated? Therefore, he himself planted the paradise of which Wisdom says: "Every planting that my Father has not planted will be rooted up" (Matthew 15:13). Good planting of angels, good saints. For saints are called under the fig tree and vine in that future time of peace, in which there is a type of angels (Micah IV, 4).

On account of the height of the kingdom he calls Babylon a "mountain" which was "ruined" from idolatry and unjust works, through which it "destroyed" the others. And it also was the city on high because of the river nearby from which some stairs went up to the city, the city being in two parts and lying close to the river on each bank, with the walls also of the city being very high. And it mentioned a "hand," the avenging power, the same power of his which destroyed something made from "rocks" for security and for watch. And due to the fire having "obliterated" its "stones," they were useless, as there was not a stone to be put together for a firm building. And for the analogical meaning, the devil is named a "mountain," as in the book of Zechariah: "Who are you, a great mountain before the face of Zerubbabel?" And concerning the one who has the "deaf and dumb" demon, the Savior said, "If you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain: 'Move away,' and it will move away." Thus the devil is a "mountain" which is "ruined" from his own evil and which "destroys" everyone to the extent they have their mind on what is earthly.

And again the Prophet Zechariah also prophesied about that stone which is Christ. For he said:—I saw a chief stone of equality and of love. And why did he say “chief”? Surely because from the beginning He was with His Father. And again that he spoke of love, it was because when He came into the world, He said thus to His disciples:—This is My commandment, that ye love one another. And again He said:—I have called you My friends (lovers). And the blessed Apostle said thus:—God loved as in the love of His Son. Of a truth Christ loved us and gave Himself for us.

And what follows: Who are you, O great mountain, before Zerubbabel? Into a plain!; they understand it as said to the devil, who stood at the right hand of Joshua to oppose him, and lifted himself up against Zerubbabel and the people of the Jews. But he has been turned into a plain and humbled, and he lies under the feet of Israel, because God shall bring out the chief stone, Christ his Son, who was always a help to the people of Israel. And his grace, that is, the grace of the stone, toward those whom he brought back from captivity, shall make equal the grace which he always exercised toward their fathers. This we have found said by the Hebrews.

But most of our writers interpret the mountain as the devil, and the Antichrist, who dares to stand before Zerubbabel, from whom Christ was to be born, and to raise himself up, and to say in the Gospel: All these things have been delivered to me, and I will give them to you, if you will fall down and worship me. And the Lord, laying him low under his feet, and making him humble instead of proud, and cast down, says: Get behind, Satan; for it is written: You shall worship the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve. And they give as an example in the Gospel the lunatic, whom the apostles had not been able to heal; they ask why they could not heal him, and they hear: Amen I say to you, if you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain: Pass from here, and it will pass; and nothing will be impossible to you. But this kind is not cast out except by prayer and fasting. There the mountain is plainly taken to mean the devil. But others, with no small rashness, refer what is plainly said of the devil to Christ, who in the holy Scriptures is quite often called a mountain. Nor is there any need to give examples, of which there is a great abundance. They are led into this error because it is written in the Seventy: Who are you, O great mountain, before the face of Zerubbabel, that you should set right? Namely, that this mountain which is before the face of Zerubbabel, that is, which descends from the stock of Zerubbabel, would himself set the world right, and that what follows is about him: I will bring out the stone of inheritance, of which it is written: It is you who will restore my inheritance to me. And in another place: He chose for us his inheritance, the beauty of Jacob whom he loved. And again: Jacob became the portion of the Lord, Israel the cord of his inheritance. And in Psalm 2: The Lord said to me: You are my Son, today I have begotten you. Ask of me, and I will give you the nations for your inheritance. But God shall bring out the chief stone, of which we read: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God, and: All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made. And what he says: He shall make equal the grace of its grace, signifies this: Of his fullness we have all received, and grace for grace, that is, for the grace of the law, the grace of the Gospel, so that both those who believe from Israel and the people of the heathen may receive an equal grace and a like gift. Hence Gabriel too says to Mary: You have found grace with the Lord. And the apostle Paul writes: For by grace you have been saved; and John the evangelist: The law, he says, was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.

Many of our writers interpret the hands of Zerubbabel, who founded the house and himself finished it, as Christ. But if we accept this, we shall be compelled to explain who the stone of tin in the hand of Zerubbabel is. For surely another Christ is not to be shown in the hand of Christ? Although some have taken the stone of tin as the body of the Lord, which was soiled by no stains of sins, and is not called lead, but purest tin.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: The hands of Zerubbabel have founded this house, and his hands shall finish it, and you shall know that the Lord of hosts has sent me to you. For who has despised the small days? And they shall rejoice, and shall see the stone of tin in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven are the eyes of the Lord, which run to and fro through the whole earth. LXX: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: The hands of Zerubbabel have founded this house, and his hands shall complete it. And you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you; for who has despised in the small days? And they shall rejoice, and shall see the stone of tin in the hand of Zerubbabel; these seven are the eyes of the Lord, which look upon all the earth. Much is said both by the Hebrews and by our writers; following most of it and rejecting some, let us set out what we think, keeping the truth of the history, so that from it we may be able to recognize him who is prophesied through the history. The hands of Zerubbabel, the prince of the Jews who returned from Babylon, laid the foundations of the temple; and his hands shall reach to the top of the temple, completing what they had begun, and building up all that had been begun. We read in Ezra that the temple was begun and finished by Zerubbabel. And when, says the prophet Zechariah, you see the roof set by you upon the temple which you are now building, then you will understand that I was sent by the Lord, and that what I have spoken I said at his command: For who has despised the small days?

Wherefore to those seven days the Lord attributed to each a thousand years; for thus went the warning: "In Thine eyes, O Lord, a thousand years are as one day." Therefore in the eyes of the Lord each thousand of years is ordained, for I find that the Lord's eyes are seven. Wherefore, as I have narrated, that true Sabbath will be in the seventh millenary of years, when Christ with His elect shall reign.
On the Creation of the World

And definitely did He show concerning this stone:—Lo! on this stone will I open seven eyes. And what then are the seven eyes that were opened on the stone? Clearly the Spirit of God that abode on Christ with seven operations, as Isaiah the Prophet said:—The Spirit of God shall rest and dwell upon Him, (a spirit) of wisdom and understanding, of counsel and of courage, of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord. These were the seven eyes that were opened upon the Stone, and these are the seven eyes of the Lord which look upon all the earth.

Here 'who' is taken for 'rare', according to that saying: Who, do you think, is the faithful and wise steward? and: Lord, who dwells in your tabernacle, and who shall go up into your holy mountain? Rare, then, is the one who despises the small days of this world and thinks royal power worth nothing. When we see the powerful of the world gleaming with gold, glowing with purple and gems, surrounded by an army, let us say within ourselves: Who, do you think, despises the small days? Hence Jacob too, understanding that the life of men is short: Small, he says, and very evil are the days of my life. Those, then, who have despised the small days — and he refers this to royal power, to admonish Zerubbabel and Joshua and the people building the temple of God, by no means to fear the adversaries who were hindering them, but to listen to the Lord exhorting them — those, from the fact that they despise royal grandeur, shall also rejoice and see the help of the Savior, who is promised from the stock of Zerubbabel, and because of his strength is called a stone, and a stone of tin. For this in the Hebrew is written abdil, because he is the wall and the strength and the might of those who believe. For just as tin defends other metals from fire, and though bronze and iron are by nature very hard, yet if it is without tin it is burned and consumed, so all the strength of angels and of men, if the help of the Savior is not there, is proved weak and frail. Now this stone, that is, this mass, which among the Hebrews is written abdil, that is, of tin, ἐτυμολογεῖται (is etymologized as) ἀποχωρίζων, that is, separating and setting apart, so that, as tin through fire parts metals that are mixed and adulterated, so the Lord, the true assayer and χωνευτὴς (refiner), may set apart the bronze and the lead of the vices from the gold and silver of good works, so that pure gold and silver may remain. In different words this ἀποχωρίζων and separator is described in the Gospel: Whose winnowing fan is in his hand, and he will cleanse his threshing floor, and will separate the chaff from the wheat, he who cries through Jeremiah: What has the chaff to do with the wheat? says the Lord.

As for the seven eyes, which run to and fro through the whole earth and judge all things, we explained above that they are the seven spirits; and that nothing is hidden from the Lord, who is aware of things past and present and to come, and renders to each according to his works, above all when he comes in the person of the one who separates the good and the wicked, and of the refiner.

Of the two olive trees which were on the right of the lamp and on the left we have read above. And so the prophet, now asking about them, does not deserve to hear, because he does not retain the former things; or else because what was said there more obscurely he desires to hear here more plainly; or at any rate his obstinacy is refuted by the angel's silence, because he insists that he knows greater things; although the Hebrews maintain that he heard nothing when he asked about the olive trees for this reason, that he did not ask well, and did not inquire into the whole of what he ought to have known. In short, afterwards he inquires more fully, adding the ears or branches of the olive trees, about which he had been silent above. For there he said: What are these two olive trees? Here he asks: What are the two ears of the olive trees? Μεταφορικῶς (metaphorically), because the trees are upright in the manner of ears of grain, and as ears are covered with their beards, so these are covered with a kind of palisade of branches and leaves, and rise up on high.

And I answered, and said to him: What are these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand, and on its left? And I answered a second time, and said to him: What are the two ears of the olive trees, which are upon the two golden beaks, in which are the pourers of gold? And he said to me, saying: Do you not know what these are? And I said: No, lord. And he said: These are the two sons of oil, who stand by the Ruler of the whole earth. LXX: And I answered, and said to him: What are these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand, and on the left? And I asked a second time, and said to him: What are the two branches of the olive trees, which are in the hands of the two golden nostrils, which pour in and draw back the golden pourers. And he said to me: Do you not know what these are? And I said: By no means, lord. And he said to me: These are the two sons of fatness, who stand by the Lord of the whole earth. When the prophet asked what the two olive trees signified, one of which stood on the right of the lampstand, the other on the left, the Lord, or the angel of the Lord, would not answer. The prophet, understanding this, inquires a second time, and said: What are the two ears of the olive trees, or the two branches? He asks about lesser things, since he did not deserve to hear the greater. Now these two branches are in the hand of the two nostrils, or upon the two golden beaks, which in Hebrew are called sinthoroth, in Greek μυξωτῆρες; and these two μυξωτῆρες themselves, upon which are the two ears, or the two branches of the olive trees, are of purest gold. And when the prophet asked also about the two branches, and was asked again by the angel whether he knew what the two branches signified, and he had said: No, lord, the angel of the Lord answered: These are the two sons of oil, as Symmachus would have it, or of στιλπνότητος, as Aquila translated, that is, of splendor; or of πιότητος, that is, of fatness, as the Seventy rendered; or of λαμπρότητος, that is, of brightness, as Theodotion translated, who stand by the Ruler of the whole earth.

Some of our writers interpret the two olive trees as the Son and the Holy Spirit, and the lamp in the middle as God the Father. But I do not know how, without blasphemy, they can take one as on the right and the other as on the left. The branches, too, or ears of the olive trees, they explain as the incarnation of the Savior and the likeness of a dove of the Holy Spirit, because we cannot see the olive trees whole, but a certain part, and, so to speak, the little branches of the incarnation of Christ and of the manifestation of the Holy Spirit have been shown to us. Others understand the two testaments, the Gospel on the right, the law on the left, because in the one there is the spiritual sense, in the other the bodily; and because we can explain neither the whole Gospel nor the whole law: And now we know in part, and we prophesy in part, and we cannot yet understand what is perfect. There are some who interpret the two branches of the olive trees, or the two ears, and the sons of fatness or of splendor, as the priesthood and the law, which afford joy to the whole earth. Others take them as Enoch and Elijah, of whom one pleased God in uncircumcision, the other in circumcision, and was caught up into heaven with his body. For splendor and oil, and fatness and brightness, we read in the Hebrew Isaar, according to what is written in the psalms of the joy and happiness of the saints: They shall be inebriated with the plenty, or with the fatness of your house: for πιότης means fatness rather than plenty. These things we have spoken as best we could, and as far as the powers of our small talent could bear, touching briefly on the various opinions both of the Hebrews and of our writers; if anyone says something better, or rather truer, we too gladly yield to what is better.

"These are the two candlesticks standing before the Lord of the earth." These two candlesticks and two olive trees He has to this end spoken of, and admonished you that if, when you have read of them elsewhere, you have not understood, you may understand here. For in Zechariah, one of the twelve prophets, it is thus written: "These are the two olive trees and two candlesticks which stand in the presence of the Lord of the earth; " that is, they are in paradise. Also, in another sense, standing in the presence of the lord of the earth, that is, in the presence of Antichrist. Therefore they must be slain by Antichrist.
Commentary on the Apocalypse of the Blessed John
5: And I turned, and lifted up my eyes, and saw, and behold, a flying scroll. And he said to me: What do you see? And I said: I see a flying scroll; its length twenty cubits, and its breadth ten cubits. And he said to me: This is the curse that goes forth over the face of the whole earth, for every thief, as it is written there, shall be judged, and everyone who swears shall likewise be judged by it. I will bring it forth, says the Lord of hosts, and it shall come to the house of the thief, and to the house of him who swears falsely by my name, and it shall remain in the midst of his house, and shall consume it, and its timbers, and its stones. LXX: And I turned, and lifted up my eyes, and saw a flying sickle. And he said to me: What do you see? And I said: I see a flying sickle, of twenty cubits in length, and ten cubits in breadth. And he said to me: This is the curse that goes forth over the face of the whole earth, for every thief shall by it be punished unto death, and every perjurer shall by it be tormented unto death. And I will bring it forth, says the Lord Almighty, and it shall enter into the house of the thief, and into the house of him who swears falsely by my name, and it shall rest in the midst of his house, and shall consume it, and its timbers, and its stones. Having turned, says the prophet, to another vision, and lifting up my eyes from joyful and happy things to sadder ones, I see a flying scroll, which in Hebrew is called megella, and was rendered by Aquila and Theodotion διφθέρα (hide), by Symmachus κεφαλὶς, that is, a heading, according to what we read in the psalm: At the head of the book it is written of me; or, according to the Seventy, Δρέπανον πετόμενον, that is, a flying sickle. For all that he had seen above had announced the building of the temple, the coming of the Lord Savior, the liberation of the people from Babylon. And so, lest his heart be lifted up, as with the Apostle — to whom was given an angel of Satan to buffet him, lest he exalt himself —, he too sees things that are sad, so that whatever arrogance had grown from the revelation of good things might shrink from the threat of sad ones. And a flying scroll is shown, in which the sins of all are written down, so that each may receive according to his works, whether good or evil, as Daniel says: Thrones were set, and the books were opened. But if we take it as a sickle, as the LXX translated, let us take an example from the Apocalypse of John, in which it is written: And the angel answered, and said to him who sat upon the horse: Put in your sharpest sickle, and reap your vineyard, for its grapes are ripe. Instead of a sickle we read in Deuteronomy of arrows and a sword: I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh. And because God did not spare the angels who sinned, who by their own fault lost their heavenly dwelling, therefore he himself says through Isaiah: My sword has been made drunk in heaven. For all the sinners of the people shall perish by the sword, not, surely, by a bodily sword — since there are many and various ways to death besides the sword —, but by a spiritual sword, with which those are to be struck who have not repented, and whom the psalmist threatens, crying out: Unless you are converted, he will brandish his sword; he has bent his bow and made it ready, and in it he has prepared the vessels of death. And in Jeremiah we read: How long will you cut, O point, or sword, of the Lord? How long will you not be still? Return into your sheath. This sword is called not only a sickle, which cuts down hay, stubble and thorns, but it is also called the axe of the trees, which will cut down those who have not brought forth fruits worthy of repentance; and of whom John the Baptist cried out: Behold, the axe is laid to the roots of the trees; every tree that does not bear good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire. This scroll, in which the sins of all are written down, or this sickle, which cuts down the offences of all, is sent into the vineyard of Sodom, of which it is written: Our enemies are without understanding, for their vine is of the vineyard of Sodom, and their shoot from Gomorrah. Their grape is a grape of gall, and theirs a cluster of bitterness. Their wine is the fury of dragons, and the incurable fury of asps. This sickle has twenty cubits of length and ten of breadth, in which number joyful things are joined with sad.
