Not that they were the same men, but that the same royal power which formerly sat in ambush with the rich, and, as though by a decree of the senate, tried to extinguish the name of Christ, now at the public expense builds the basilicas of the churches and raises their highest gables, so as not only to adorn ceilings and roofs gleaming with gold, but to clothe the walls with veneers of varied marble; and the divine books which formerly it handed over to burning, it now venerates, gilded and purpled and set off with a variety of gems, for the safekeeping of the Roman state.

Thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I will save my people from the land of the east and from the land of the setting of the sun. And I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in justice. LXX: likewise. Some of the Jews say that these things were fulfilled after Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, when the temple had been built, the walls of the city raised and the Jewish state restored, by the Maccabees and the various princes who ruled Judea down to Herod. Others relate that they are to be fulfilled at the consummation of the world under the Christ, for whom they wait in vain. But we say that they were both partly fulfilled at that time, that is, after Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, and went before as it were in types and images, when the people was brought back from captivity and dwelt in Jerusalem and was called the people of God, and the Lord was again called their God, by no means in falsehood and iniquity but in truth and justice; and that now, most fully, under the Lord and Savior in the Church, that is, in the true Jerusalem, the promise is fulfilled in deed, especially because it is said: Behold, I will save my people from the land of the east and from the land of the west; of whom the Lord also spoke in the Gospel: Many shall come from the east and the west, and shall recline in the kingdom of heaven with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. And long before, the psalmist had promised, saying: The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken, and has called the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting. Out of Zion the loveliness of his beauty. For there shall come out of Zion one to rescue and to overturn iniquities from Jacob, when from the east and the west incense is offered to the name of the Lord in every place, and a pure sacrifice, by no means in the victims of the Old Testament, but in the holiness of evangelical purity; of which incense we read elsewhere too: Let my prayer be directed as incense in your sight. And what this incense is, the words that follow show: The lifting up of my hands an evening sacrifice. For after there sprang up from the rod of Jesse one who should rule the nations, and in him the nations hoped, and from the east and from the west both the first people and the last believed in the Lord, and there was made one flock, then all the nations were called to gladness and stirred to joy, as the prophet says: Rejoice, you nations, with his people. According to what is written elsewhere: All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations shall worship before him.

Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?  And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?  And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? for ye are the temple of the living God; as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. [Zechariah 8:8] Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you,  And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.

And what follows, In truth and justice, signifies that the shadow of the old law departs and the truth of the Gospel comes, by no means in the justice of the Jews, but in Christian justice; for the Lord himself is truth and justice, of whom we read: Truth has risen from the earth, and justice has looked down from heaven. Hence in Psalm 14 (15) too justice and truth are named together: He who walks without blemish and works justice, and speaks truth in his heart.

Thus says the Lord of hosts: Let your hands be strengthened, you who hear in these days these words through the mouth of the prophets, on the day on which the house of the Lord of hosts was founded, that the temple might be built. The Seventy translated "the Lord Almighty" for "the Lord of hosts", the rest likewise. The temple having been built under Zerubbabel and Joshua (for it was in the fourth year of King Darius, on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is called Chislev), all these things are said when the temple had already been raised; the same prophets, Haggai and Zechariah, who had exhorted both the leaders and the people that it might be built, now exhort them, so that from the truth of the earlier things they may lend faith to those which are promised for the future; and that they may strengthen their hands, in no way fearing the onset of the Medes and the plots of the surrounding nations who desire to hinder them; and that they may be strengthened through the mouth of the prophets, from the day on which the foundations of the temple were laid until the day on which the temple was built up on them, and may hear what follows. We explain the history briefly, referring spiritually to the Church whatever is said of Jerusalem and of the temple: in the Church hands are strengthened through good works, and houses are founded when the foundations of faith are laid, and the temple is raised when the multitude of believers is made firm, and lives in such a way that it deserves to be the temple of God.

For before those days there was no wage for men, nor was there a wage for beasts, nor was there peace for him who came in and went out, because of the tribulation; and I let loose all men, each one against his neighbor. LXX: For before those days the wage of men shall not be for gain, and the wage of beasts shall not stand, and for him who goes out and him who comes in there shall be no peace because of the tribulation; and I will send forth all men, each one to his neighbor. The Seventy referred everything to future time, but it is better referred to the past, as it stands in the Hebrew, and the truth of the exposition will bear this out. Before the house of the Lord was founded and the temple of the Lord was built, all your labor was in vain. And men as well as beasts, in farming, in trading and in various works, were frustrated in empty efforts; enemies abroad and sedition at home disturbed the peace, and everywhere there was a standstill of public business because of the frequency of wars and the plots at home, while brother keeps no faith with brother, and all kinship is hostile. Haggai the prophet, embracing this sense in other words, says: And now set your hearts from this day and upward, before stone was laid upon stone in the temple of the Lord. When you came to a heap of twenty measures, and they became ten; and you went in to the winepress to press out fifty flagons, and they became twenty. I struck you with a burning wind and with blight, and with hail all the works of your hands, and there was none among you who would return to me, says the Lord; and this we can take both of the Church and of each one of the believers. For before the foundations of the house of God are laid in us, and we are built up as a temple for God, and hear from the Apostle: You are the temple of God, and the Holy Spirit dwells in you; whatever good work we seemed to have, whether as rational beings, who are called men, or as simple ones, who are called beasts — For men and beasts, he says, you will save, O Lord — has no wage with God; and there are wars and discords in us, and tribulation everywhere, and we are without the peace of Christ, which, as he went to the Father, he left to the apostles; and the Lord's saying is fulfilled in us: A man's enemies are those of his own household. For every brother supplants with supplanting; and every friend walks deceitfully, and a man mocks his brother and does not speak the truth; their tongue has learned to speak a lie. But if we turn to Christ and are made his temple, at once we shall hear the Apostle proclaiming: Each one shall receive his own wage according to his work.

But now I will not deal with the remnant of this people as in the former days, says the Lord of hosts, but there shall be a seed of peace. The vine shall give its fruit and the earth shall give its shoot; and the heavens shall give their dew, and I will cause the remnant of this people to possess all these things. LXX: And now I will not deal with the remnant of this people as in the former days, says the Lord Almighty, but I will show peace. The vine shall give its fruit and the earth shall give its shoots; and heaven shall give its dew, and I will cause the remnant of my people to possess all these things. Before the foundations of the house of God were laid and the temple was built, there was no wage for men, nor a wage for beasts, nor, because of tribulation and distress, peace for those who came in and went out, and all men were at variance among themselves with hostile hatred. But now, since the foundations of the house of the Lord have already been laid and the temple has been built, I will by no means do as I had done before to those who have returned from the Babylonian captivity; but there shall be peace and joy everywhere, and the abundance to come will make up for the drought and famine of the former time. For the vine shall give its fruit, and all the winepresses shall be filled, the earth shall be clothed with glad crops, and with the rains and the night dew watering it, all things shall sprout; all that I have said, I will cause the remnant of my people to possess; the foundations of the house of the Lord have been laid, and the temple has been raised. The prophet Haggai too speaks these same things at the same time, who had said above: I struck you with a burning wind and with blight and with hail all the works of your hands. After the foundations of the temple were laid: Set, he says, in your hearts from this day and into the future, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, from the day on which the foundations of the temple were laid, set it upon your heart. Is the seed already in the shoot, and has the vine and the fig and the pomegranate and the olive tree yet flowered? From this day I will bless, and again I will move heaven and earth alike. Let us also say it another way, following the explanation begun concerning the Church. Before anyone receives the faith of Christ, and the foundations of the Holy Spirit are laid in him, no one will be able to hear: There is a wage for your work. Whether he be a Jew, or a heretic, or a Gentile, whatever good work he has done, unless he has done it in the name of Christ, he will not have the wage of his good work. We see the virgins of the heretics, the rigor of the philosophers, the observance of the Jews in the variety of foods, and yet we say, according to Haggai, that they eat and are not satisfied; they drink and are not made drunk; they are covered and are not warmed; and he who gathers wages puts them into a bag with holes. But after they have received the faith of Christ, both those and these who had been sinners in the Church, and for the greatness of their offenses had been handed over to the captivity of this world and burned by the Babylonian fire, and have heard the Lord preaching: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to preach the gospel to the poor, to proclaim release to the captives, and sight to the blind, to heal those who are of a contrite heart, and when that which is said through Amos has been fulfilled in them: I will turn back the captivity of my people Israel, and they shall build the ruined cities, and I will plant them, then in those days justice shall rise, and abundance of peace.

The vine shall give its fruit, the vine that says in the Gospel: I am the vine, you are the branches. Every branch that abides in me, the Father cleanses, that it may bear greater fruit. And when its branches have been cleansed, that is, its shoots and layers, and with budding eyes have begun to promise the hope of fruits to come, so that what is written may be fulfilled: The flowering vines have given forth their fragrance, then the sun of justice has colored the hanging clusters, so that, sent into the winepresses of Psalms 8 and 83 (84), which are entitled for the winepresses, they may be trodden by the foot of the Lord, who comes up from Bozrah, that he may pour out the wine that gladdens the heart of man. The earth too shall give its shoot, not the dry and stony earth full of thorns, but the good earth which yields fruit a hundredfold and sixtyfold and thirtyfold, so that those who have sown in tears may reap in joy. But the heavens too shall give their dew, the heavens of which it is written in Psalm 18 (19): The heavens tell the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the works of his hands. Of these heavens it is said in the song of Deuteronomy: Rejoice, O heavens, with him, that is, with the Lord and Savior, whom he foreknew and predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son; it is he who speaks with Moses: Let my speech be awaited like the rain, and let my words come down like the dew. For those who were dead in sins shall rise again, and those who lay in whitewashed sepulchres, which are full of dead men's bones, shall be raised up, and those who dwell in the earth shall rejoice. And what the cause of the joy is, the following words show: For the dew which is from you is their healing. And all these things, namely peace and the fruit of the vines, and the abundance of the lands, which has grown up from the dew of the heavens, the remnant of my people shall possess, of whom Isaiah speaks: Unless the Lord Sabaoth had left us a seed, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like Gomorrah. For the remnant according to the election of grace has been saved, not by works, otherwise grace would not be grace.

But concerning the Church and each one of the believers it can be understood thus: that in the time of persecution the Christians were a curse and an example to all the nations round about, because they had offended their Lord; and afterwards they are in blessing, when peace has been restored; and all this comes about because the Lord, who had at first been angry, afterwards has mercy on Jerusalem, the vision of peace, and on Judah, which confesses the faith of the Lord. Each of the believers, too, who are cast out of the Church for their vices and are handed over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that they may learn not to blaspheme, when they have done repentance, will return to their former state and will see the peace of the Lord, and will possess the glory of their confession.

And it shall be: as you were a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you and you shall be a blessing: do not fear, let your hands be strengthened. For thus says the Lord of hosts: As I purposed to afflict you, when your fathers had provoked me to anger, says the Lord, and I did not have mercy, so, having turned, I have purposed in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah: do not fear. LXX: And it shall be: as you were in a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you shall be in a blessing; take courage and be strengthened in your hearts, for thus says the Lord Almighty. As I purposed to afflict you in that your fathers had provoked me to anger, says the Lord Almighty, and I did not repent, so I am ready and have purposed in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah: take courage. He promises these things as to come after the building of the temple: that as the house of Judah and the house of Israel, namely the two and the ten tribes, were among all the nations a curse and a hissing and an example, so, when they have been saved and have returned to Judea, they may be a blessing to all. Do not fear, he says, the adversaries who rebel; be confident that what the Lord promises through me is true, let your hands be strengthened, finish the works which you have begun.

The cause of the strengthening is the Lord's promise: For thus says the Lord Almighty, to whom nothing is impossible, who is able to fulfil what he promises: As I devised to afflict you and to hand you over to captivity, because your fathers provoked me to anger, and I did not have mercy, which the LXX translated οὐ μετενόησα, that is, I did not repent, which in Hebrew is written ulo naamathi; but I did not have mercy, so that I might correct you by captivity and train you through every torment and scourge; so now, in the present time, I have purposed to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. And it is to be noted that when he is angry, the house of Judah and the house of Israel, that is, all twelve tribes which were handed over to captivity, are a curse among the nations. But after he has purposed to do good, he does not do it to Judah and Israel, that is, to the two and the ten tribes, namely to Jerusalem and Samaria, Oholah and Oholibah; but, leaving Israel in captivity, he does good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. And he adds at the end: Do not fear, or take courage, in the sense which we have explained above.

What is written, I did not have mercy, or I did not repent, the heretics slander, as though the Lord were either cruel or changeable, if he either does not repent or repents. For if he has repented, they say that he is changeable; if he has not repented, they assert that he is cruel. Yet God repented that he had anointed Saul as king. And among the Ninevites, to whom he had announced through the prophet: Yet three days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown, because they did repentance, he himself too is said to have changed his sentence, not through the fault of an improvident mind, but from the difference in what they do, badly or well. For if they do evil, he threatens; if they have blotted out their former sins, he has mercy; God is not changed, who is one and the same and cannot be changed, but when they have changed from evil to good works, he himself also changes his own decree. He it is who also speaks in Genesis: The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has been multiplied, and their sins are exceedingly great; I will go down, therefore, and see whether they are fulfilling it according to their cry which has come to me; and if not, that I may know. What he said is this: If they persist in their fury, punishment will not be lacking to the sinners; if they cease from their madness, they will become most worthy of my knowledge. For the Lord knows those who are his. And the Apostle writes to the Galatians: But then, not knowing God. And although God knows all, and nothing past, nor present, nor future is hidden from him, in the Gospel he says that he does not know the wicked: Depart from me, workers of iniquity, I do not know you. Therefore let us take both the knowledge and the repentance, and the wrath and indignation, and all the affections of God, not according to the defect of human speech, but according to the sense of the divine majesty.

This I say therefore, and testify in the Lord, that ye henceforth walk not as other Gentiles walk, in the vanity of their mind,  Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their heart:  Who being past feeling have given themselves over unto lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness.  But ye have not so learned Christ;  If so be that ye have heard him, and have been taught by him, as the truth is in Jesus:  That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts;  And be renewed in the spirit of your mind;  And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.  Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another. [Zechariah 8:16] Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath:  Neither give place to the devil.  Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.  Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers.  And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.  Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice:  And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.

[Burnt offerings] he accordingly did away with, so that the new law of our Lord Jesus Christ might be without restraining yoke and without manmade offering. Again he says to them, "Did I command your fathers when they came out of the land of Egypt to offer me burnt offerings and sacrifices? Rather I did command them this: Let none of you cherish evil in his heart against his neighbor, and do not love a false oath." We ought therefore to understand, if we are not senseless, the kindly intention of our Father, for he speaks to us, desiring us not to err like them but to seek how to make our offering to him. To us he accordingly speaks thus: "A contrite heart is a sacrifice to the Lord; an odor of sweetness to the Lord is a heart which glorifies its maker."  We ought, therefore, to watch carefully after our salvation, brothers, lest the evil one, sneaking in among us deceitfully, push us away from our life.

For indeed there is nothing equal to this virtue. Wouldest thou learn the power of this virtue? "Though Moses and Samuel stood before Me," saith God, "my soul would not regard them." Nevertheless, those whom Moses and Samuel were not able to snatch away from God's wrath, this precept when observed was able to snatch away. Hence it is, that He continually exhorts those to whom He had spoken these things, saying, "Let none of you revengefully imagine evil against his brother in your heart," and "let none of you think of his neighbour's malice." It is not said merely, forego wrath; but retain it not in thy mind; think not of it; part with all thy resentment; do away the sore. For thou supposest that thou art paying him back the injury; but thou art first tormenting thyself, and setting up thy rage as an executioner within thee in every part, and tearing up thine own bowels. For what can be more wretched than a man perpetually angry? And just as maniacs, who never enjoy tranquility, so also he who is resentful, and retains an enemy, will never have the enjoyment of any peace; incessantly raging, as he does, and daily increasing the tempest of his thoughts, calling to mind his words and acts, and detesting the very name of him who has aggrieved him. Do you but mention his enemy, he becomes furious at once, and sustains much inward anguish; and should he chance to get only a bare sight of him, he fears and trembles, as if encountering the worst evils. Yea, if he perceives any of his relations, if but his garment, or his dwelling, or street, he is tormented by the sight of them.

These, then, are the words which you shall do: Speak the truth, each one with his neighbor; judge truth and the judgment of peace in your gates; and let none of you devise evil in your hearts against his friend, and do not love a lying oath; for all these are things that I hate, says the Lord. LXX: These are the words which you shall do: Speak the truth, each one with his neighbor, and a peaceable judgment, judge in your gates, and let each one not devise evil against his neighbor in your hearts, and do not love a lying oath, for all these things I hate, says the Lord Almighty. I have promised that I will not deal with the remnant of the people of the captives as in the former days. And as I purposed to afflict them, when their fathers had provoked me to anger, and I did not have mercy, so now, having turned, I have purposed in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. So that my sentence, then, may stand, and the promise may not be made void, do these things which I command: Speak the truth with your neighbors. Let us take neighbor to mean the whole race of men, since we have been begotten of one parent; otherwise, if neighbor is taken to mean kinsman, we must lie to strangers and foreigners. The Apostle says this same thing: Putting away lying, speak the truth, each one with his neighbor. Truth, he says, and the judgment of peace judge in your gates. In judgment let truth and justice come first; then mercy follows. For this is the judgment of peace: that the judge should have as his purpose to make peace between those at variance, according to that saying of the Gospel: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God. And what follows, In your gates, agrees with that prophetic saying: They hated him who reproves in the gates, and they abhorred the holy word. And in another place: They shall not be put to shame when they speak with their enemies in the gate. David too used to judge in the gates, when Absalom, promising the truth of judgment, was laying a trap for his father. And it is asked why among the Jews the place of judging was in the gates. So that the farmers should not be forced to enter the cities and undergo some loss, the judges sat in the gates, so that they might hear townsmen and countrymen alike at the going out and coming in of the city, and when the business was finished, each might at once return to his own dwelling.

And do not devise evil, he says, against your friends in your hearts; raath, which all with one voice have translated κακίαν, that is, evil, we can take in two ways, both for affliction and for wickedness. For affliction: If there is evil in a city which the Lord has not done, and: Sufficient for the day is its own evil. For wickedness, God speaks in the prophet Jonah: The cry of their evil has gone up to me, and in the Apostle we read: Filled with all iniquity and evil. In both ways, therefore, he who is holy neither afflicts his friend nor devises evil against him in his heart. And do not love, he says, a lying oath; for the Lord commands in the Gospel: But I say to you, do not swear at all, but let your speech be, yes yes, no no; for he who does not swear will never be able to swear falsely. Let him who swears hear what is written: You shall not take up the name of the Lord your God in a vain thing. All these are things that I hate, says the Lord, according to the words of Malachi, who says: And all the things that I hated, you did. In precepts which pertain to life and are plain, we ought not to look for allegory, lest, as the Comic poet says, we seek a knot in a bulrush.

Therefore let us also, when we come to the feast, no longer come as to old shadows, for they are accomplished, neither as to common feasts, but let us hasten as to the Lord, Who is Himself the feast, not looking upon it as an indulgence and delight of the belly, but as a manifestation of virtue. For the feasts of the heathen are full of greediness, and utter indolence, since they consider they celebrate a feast when they are idle; and they work the works of perdition when they feast. But our feasts consist in the exercise of virtue and the practice of temperance; as the prophetic word testifies in a certain place, saying, ‘The fast of the fourth, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth [month], shall be to the house of Judah for gladness, and rejoicing, and for pleasant feasts.’ Since therefore this occasion for exercise is set before us, and such a day as this is come, and the prophetic voice has gone forth that the feast shall be celebrated, let us give all diligence to this good proclamation, and like those who contend on the race course, let us vie with each other in observing the purity of the fast, by watchfulness in prayers, by study of the Scriptures, by distributing to the poor, and let us be at peace with our enemies.

And the word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: The fast of the fourth, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth shall be to the house of Judah for joy and for gladness, and for glorious solemn feasts; only love truth and peace. LXX: And the word of the Lord Almighty came to me, saying: Thus says the Lord Almighty: The fourth fast, and the fifth fast, and the seventh fast, and the tenth fast shall be to the house of Judah for joy and for gladness, and for good festivals; — for in Hebrew this is said tobim, that is, ἀγαθάς —, and rejoice, and love truth and peace. To what Sharezer and Regem-melech had asked above through envoys, whether they ought to fast and lament in the fifth month and in the seventh month, as it stands in the LXX, or after the building of the temple to end the fast and lay aside their mourning, the prophet, after many things have been set out in between which they were to do and which they were to hope for, answered in the person of the Lord: The fast of the fourth, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth — for month is understood ἀπὸ κοινοῦ (from the shared word) —, to the house of Judah, and to Jerusalem, shall be turned into festal days and joy. God seeks only truth and peace. On this passage many of our writers have said many things, and things at variance with one another. Some, confessing the obscurity by their silence, have passed over it in their commentaries as though it were a very deep pit, judging it more right to say nothing at all than to say too little. We are therefore compelled to have recourse to the Hebrews, and to seek the truth of knowledge from the spring rather than from the streams, especially since this is not some prophecy of Christ, where they are wont to dodge and to hide the truth with a lie, but the order of a history woven from what precedes and what follows. The fast of the fourth month, which among the Latins is called July, on the seventeenth day of that same month, they think was the day when Moses, coming down from Mount Sinai, threw down and broke the tablets of the law; and, according to Jeremiah, the walls of the city were first breached. In the fifth month, which among the Latins is called August, when because of the spies of the holy land a sedition had arisen among the people, they were ordered not to go up the mountain but for forty years to go round toward the holy land by long and wasteful wanderings, so that, except for two, Caleb and Joshua, all fell in the wilderness. In this month the temple at Jerusalem was burned and destroyed, both by Nebuchadnezzar and, many ages later, by Titus and Vespasian; the city of Bether was taken, to which many thousands of the Jews had fled; the temple was ploughed up by Turannius Rufus to the disgrace of the oppressed nation. And in the seventh, which among us is called October, as we said above, Gedaliah was slain, and the remnant of the tribe of Judah and of Jerusalem was scattered. Let us read Jeremiah. In the tenth month, which among us is called January, because it is the door of the year and its beginning, Ezekiel, set in captivity, heard, and all the people of the captives, that in the fifth month the temple had been overthrown, as we learn most fully in that same prophet. This, then, is the whole of what is said: The days of lamentation and of fasts which until now you have kept in mourning, know that, since I have purposed to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah, they are to be turned for you into gladness and joy and solemn feasts; provided only that you love truth and peace. According to ἀναγωγὴν (anagogy): since we fast when the bridegroom is taken away from us and we do not deserve to have his presence, when the Lord has returned to us and has purposed to do good to us, all sadness shall be turned into joy; and the former famine of the word of God shall be made up for by the presence of his teachings and the fullness of the heavenly bread.

Thus says the Lord of hosts: Until peoples come, and dwell in many cities, and the inhabitants go one to another, saying: Let us go and entreat the face of the Lord, and let us seek the Lord of hosts. I too will go, and many peoples and strong nations shall come to seek the Lord of hosts in Jerusalem, and to entreat the face of the Lord. LXX: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Many peoples shall yet come, and the inhabitants of many cities; and those who dwell in the cities shall be gathered into one city, saying: Let us go to entreat the face of the Lord, and let us seek the countenance of the Lord Almighty. I too will go, and many peoples and very many nations shall come, to seek the face of the Lord Almighty in Jerusalem, and to entreat the face of the Lord. The fast of the fourth, and of the fifth, and of the seventh, and of the tenth month shall be changed into excellent solemn feasts, so much so that the cities of Judea which before were deserted shall be thronged with many inhabitants; and one city shall go to another, and they shall exhort one another and say: Because for these seventy years the ways of Zion mourned, since there was no one to go to the solemn feast, all her gates deserted, and her priests groaning, now that peace has been restored, let us go to Jerusalem, where it is commanded in the law that we should sacrifice victims, and that three times in the year every male of ours should appear in the sight of the Lord; and when one city says to another: Let us go and entreat the face of the Lord, and let us seek the Lord Almighty, the other city will answer: I too will go: at which time many peoples and countless and strong nations shall come, to offer sacrifices in Jerusalem to the Lord of hosts, and to entreat his face. For the Lord draws near to those who do not tempt him, and shows his face to those who are not unbelieving. He who has seen the Son sees the Father also; and the Lord and Savior is the image of the invisible God, not that the Son is visible and the Father invisible, but that when the Son is named, the Father is perceived. For he is by no means Father if he has no Son. Hence he himself also says in the Gospel: Father, I have manifested your name to men. What we said of Jerusalem and Zerubbabel, or of the time after Zerubbabel, is more rightly and more fully referred to Christ and to Jerusalem, which is understood as the Church; and that then from the whole world both peoples and nations will flock together to offer sacrifices in the temple of the Lord. In a time of persecution also, as we touched on briefly before, let the teachers and priests of the Church boldly promise the captives and the believers that the παροικίαι (sojourning communities) are to be built again, and the tranquillity of peace restored, and the face of the Lord entreated in the churches. We run quickly over what is plain, so as to linger over what is more obscure.
The whole life of a good Christian is a holy longing to make progress.

Thus says the Lord of hosts: In those days, in which ten men of all the tongues of the nations shall take hold, and they shall take hold of the hem of a man who is a Jew, saying: We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you. LXX: Thus says the Lord Almighty: In those days, if ten men of all the tongues of the nations take hold, and grasp the hem of a man who is a Jew, saying: We will go with you, because we have heard that God is with you. Some of the Jews say that these things were fulfilled under Zerubbabel and after Zerubbabel. Others put them off to a future time, when they hope that the Christ will come. But we understand them both more rightly and more truly of the coming of the Lord and Savior, when he was born of the virgin Mary. In short, it is written: Until peoples come? When it says until, it signifies not the present time, in which Zerubbabel and Joshua were, but the future, when many peoples and strong nations shall come, to seek the Lord of hosts in Jerusalem, and to entreat the face of the Lord. At that time, therefore, and in those days, ten men of all the tongues of the nations shall take hold of the hem of a man who is a Jew, saying: We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you. And in Isaiah we read: Seven women shall take hold of one man, saying: We will eat our own bread and be clothed with our own garments; only let your name be called upon us, take away our reproach. Those, then, who there are called seven women, that is, Churches, whose number is contained also in the apostle Paul — for he writes to seven churches, to the Romans, to the Corinthians, to the Galatians, to the Ephesians, to the Philippians, to the Colossians, to the Thessalonians. And in the Apocalypse of John the Lord, girded with variety and with purest gold, walks in the midst of the seven lampstands, that is, of the churches of the Ephesians, the Smyrnaeans, the Pergamenes, the Thyatirans, the Sardians, the Philadelphians, the Laodiceans —, are now named ten in the prophet Zechariah, whom the Lord also sought, so that, if he had found them in Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, he might deliver them from destruction. For the letter iota, with which the name of the Savior takes its beginning, signifies the number ten not only among the Greeks but also among the Hebrews. And by this mystical language it is shown that all who are counted under the name of Christian, whom the Lord also says he left, seven thousand, in the time of the persecution of Jezebel and the flight of Elijah, who did not bow the knee before Baal, and who have come to the measure of the perfect man out of all tongues and nations, shall take hold of the hem of a man who is a Jew, that is, of the Lord and Savior, of whom it is also said in the psalm: Judah is my king, and: Judah, your brothers shall praise you, and again: A prince shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until he comes for whom it is laid up; and he shall be the expectation of the nations. For there shall be the root of Jesse, and he who shall rise up to rule the nations, in him the nations shall hope. And when they have taken hold of him, they will long to cling to his footsteps, since God is with him. Or else, whoever out of all tongues and nations have believed shall take hold of a man who is a Jew, the apostles who are of the Jews, and shall say: Let us go with you; for we have heard through the prophets, and have learned by the voice of all the Scriptures, that the Son of God, Christ, God and Lord, is with you. Where the prophecy is most manifest, and the coming of Christ and of his apostles and the faith of all the nations are proclaimed, let us seek nothing further. As for our having said that the number seven thousand pertains to the name of Christians, reckon in Greek ἑπτάκεις χιλίους (seven thousand) and χριστειανούς (Christians), and you will find the same number and sum, that is, one thousand nine hundred and forty-one. But they also refer to the mystery of this number the parable of the ten virgins in the Gospel, whom we interpret of the senses of the flesh and of the spirit, if they have prepared the oil of good works for their lamps, and have doubled the number five, so as to be holy, according to the Apostle, in body and in spirit. So too the ten cities, which he who has governed the senses of the body excellently shall receive in the future, the number doubled.

God will make the return of the remainder so conspicuous that many people who are from different nations and have shared that calamity will perceive God's care for the people. They will lay hold of any one of them and use him as a guide for a return to Jerusalem, since everyone is sufficiently stirred up to that end from the clear realization that God is with them on the basis of the incredible deeds done for them. The phrase "ten men," note, here too refers not to number but has the meaning of many.
9: The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Hadrach, and of Damascus his rest, for the eye of man is the Lord's, and of all the tribes of Israel. LXX: The taking up of the word of the Lord in the land of Sedrach and of Damascus his sacrifice, for the Lord looks upon men, and all the tribes of Israel. This whole vision, or weight and burden of the word of the Lord, as Aquila translated it, pertains to the calling of the nations and the building of the Church. And the order of the words is: The taking up of the word of the Lord, sharp toward sinners, soft toward the just. For Hadrach, a name compounded of two whole words, sounds this: ad meaning sharp, rach soft and tender, and not, as it is wrongly read by some, Sedrach. Some refer Hadrach to the people of the Jews, Damascus to the calling of the nations. Hence the people, or the taking up of the word of the Lord, comes about in the land of Hadrach, over which the Lord exercised both his severity and his clemency: severity toward those who would not believe, clemency toward those who returned with the apostles; but Damascus is properly the rest of the Lord, according to what is written in Isaiah: And his rest shall be honor. For before the child knew how to choose good or evil and to call father and mother, he received the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria. Hence Damascus too is rendered in our language drinking blood, or blood of sackcloth, so that the first interpretation signifies a bloodthirsty people, the second repentance joined to its cruelty. And what follows: For the eye of man is the Lord's and of all the tribes of Israel, they expound thus: For this reason the temple of God is to be built from both peoples, that is, both from the land of Hadrach and from Damascus his rest, because whoever looks to God and hopes in him, both from the nations and from all the tribes of Israel, is the Lord's; or, according to the LXX, because the Lord looks equally upon all men, and upon all the tribes of Israel. Let us also say it another way: In the land of Hadrach is the burden of the word of the Lord, and a most heavy weight. But in Damascus are his victims and sacrifice, for the Lord looks upon both the faith of the nations and the faithlessness of the circumcision without any respect of persons, and is equally the God of all, laying the heavy weight of his sentence upon some, and resting in the seat of others. The Jews say that all these things are to be fulfilled at the coming of the Christ, whom they promise themselves in the last time, so that both the land of Hadrach and Damascus, and Hamath and Tyre, and Sidon and Ashkelon and Gaza, Ekron also and Ashdod and the Philistines, shall bow their necks to a most mighty king and serve him as he dwells in Jerusalem, and that no one shall dare to raise a hand against Israel, all around being at peace. All of which we show to have been accomplished spiritually at the coming of the Lord and in his Churches.

But Tyre and Sidon — of which the one is interpreted συνοχὴ, that is, distress, the other θήρευμα, that is, hunting —, took to themselves wisdom to such a degree that, with its sophisms and the nets of dialectic and the webs of the sophists, which Scripture calls fortifications, Tyre put riddles to Solomon, that is, to the peaceful king; and gathered its silver, namely the brilliance of eloquence, and its gold, the cunning of its thoughts, like the dust and mud that lie in the streets and roads, so as to possess the kingdom of idolatry that it had fortified. But against these fortifications the Apostle speaks: For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty to God for the destruction of fortifications, destroying reasonings and every height that exalts itself against the knowledge of God. And under the figure of Nineveh, which is interpreted adorned, or beautiful, for nothing is more adorned than the world, the word of God is directed through the prophet against the men of the world: And you shall be made drunk, and shall be despised, and you shall seek help from the enemy; all your fortifications are like a fig tree with its early figs: if they are shaken, they shall fall into the mouth of the eater.

Hamath also on its borders, and Tyre and Sidon, for they have taken to themselves exceeding wisdom. And Tyre built her fortification, and heaped up silver like dust, and gold like the mud of the streets. Behold, the Lord shall possess her, and shall strike her strength in the sea, and she shall be devoured by fire. LXX: And Hamath on its borders, Tyre and Sidon, since they were exceedingly wise, and Tyre built her fortification, and gathered silver like dust, and gold like the mud of the roads. Therefore the Lord shall possess her, and shall strike her strength in the sea, and she shall be burned up in fire. Hamath, which is interpreted χόλος, that is, wrath, is the same city that received the name Epiphania from Antiochus Ἐπιφανεῖ (Epiphanes), and is now a city of Coele Syria. This one, therefore, and Tyre and Sidon shall be within the borders of Damascus, or within the borders of the land of Hadrach, so as to believe in the Lord and Savior, to whom it was said by the Father: Ask of me, and I will give you the nations for your inheritance, and the ends of the earth for your possession. The daughters of this Tyre, that is, the souls that believe in Christ, shall bring gifts to the king, that what is written may be fulfilled: The daughters of Tyre shall worship him with gifts. And when the city of God, the Church, has been built, of which the psalmist sings: Glorious things are spoken of you, city of God, at once the rest will follow: Behold the foreigners, and Tyre, and the people of the Ethiopians, these were born there. Of the foreigners it is said in two psalms: Foreigners serve me, or are subject. Of the Ethiopians we read in the prophet Zephaniah: From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia they shall bring gifts to me, and in the psalm: Ethiopia shall stretch out her hands first to God. And of Tyre the Gospel speaks: Woe to you, Chorazin, woe to you, Bethsaida; for if the mighty works that were done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, perhaps they would long ago have repented in sackcloth and ashes. From the borders of Tyre and Sidon that Canaanite woman, the Syrophoenician, whose daughter was badly afflicted by a demon, came to meet the Lord and Savior; and she dedicated the first fruits of the faith of the Tyrians and Sidonians, so that those who had not believed in the time of Christ, because they had not yet seen the signs and mighty works, should afterwards see them through the apostles and believe, and should share in that blessedness which the Lord promises, saying: More blessed are those who have not seen and have believed.

Many, I know, respect the Jews and think that their present way of life is a venerable one. This is why I hasten to uproot and tear out this deadly opinion. I said that the synagogue is no better than a theater, and I bring forward a prophet as my witness. Surely the Jews are not more deserving of belief than their prophets. "You had a harlot's brow; you became shameless before all." Where a harlot has set herself up, that place is a brothel and a theater; it also is a den of robbers and a lodging for wild beasts. Jeremiah said, "Your house has become for me the den of a hyena." He does not simply say "of a wild beast" but "of a filthy wild beast," and again, "I have abandoned my house, I have cast off my inheritance." But when God forsakes a place, that place becomes the dwelling of demons.

And so the Lord shall possess both Tyre and Sidon, when he has first struck their strength in the most salt and most bitter sea of this world; and, lest anything of their former wisdom remain in them, that is, of the swollen folly through which they procured for themselves feeble fortifications, and silver and gold like mud, he will smelt them with fire and cleanse them to purity; of which the Savior speaks in the Gospel: I came to cast fire upon the earth, and how I wish that it were kindled, according to what is written in Mark: Everyone shall be salted with fire.

Ashkelon shall see and fear, and Gaza, and shall grieve exceedingly; and Ekron, because her hope is confounded, and the king shall perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon shall not be inhabited. And the separator shall sit in Ashdod, and I will destroy the pride of the Philistines. And I will take away his blood from his mouth and his abominations from between his teeth, and he too shall be left to our God, and he shall be as a leader in Judah, and Ekron as the Jebusite. And I will surround my house with those who fight as soldiers for me, going and returning, and the exactor shall no more pass over them, for now I have seen with my eyes. LXX: Ashkelon shall see and fear, and Gaza, and shall grieve exceedingly; and Ekron, because she is confounded in her hope, and the king shall perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon shall not be inhabited. And foreigners shall dwell in Ashdod, and I will destroy the insolence of the foreigners, and I will take away their blood from their mouth, and their abominations from between their teeth, and these too shall remain to our God, and they shall be as a χιλίαρχος, that is, tribune, in Judah, and Ekron as the Jebusite; and I will set up a height in my house, so that no one may pass through, or return, and no driver-off and towering one shall come upon them any more, for now I have seen with my eyes. Ashkelon is interpreted ignoble fire, or weighed; Gaza, strong, or rule; Ekron, barren, or uprooted; Ashdod, which in Hebrew is called Esdod, generating fire, or fire of the paternal uncle, or fire of the breast; Jebusite sounds trodden down. We have set out the etymologies of the names in order to run briefly through the sense. Ashkelon and Gaza and Ekron, seeing that Hamath was within the borders of Damascus, and that Tyre and Sidon, after they were struck round about, and all their hay, wood and stubble burned up in the conflagration, were possessed by the Lord; they too, terrified by fear and grief and confusion, began to hope for better things. In short, Ashkelon, in which there was before the ignoble fire of the devil, and which had come to the full measure and weight of sins, trembled with dread because she ceased to have inhabitants. And Gaza grieved exceedingly, doing penance for her former crimes, she who had once been strong and hard, untamable, and had promised herself the rule over all, because her king and princes, the contrary word and the power of the enemy, had lost their rule. Ekron too, barren because without the law and the knowledge of God she had no sons, was uprooted, so that she might hear that prophetic word: Rejoice, barren one who do not bear; break forth and cry, you who are not in labor, for many more are the sons of the desolate than of her who has a husband.

And when Ashkelon, Gaza and Ekron have been terrified, and have grieved because they either had no inhabitants, or lost their king, or their former hope was frustrated, foreigners shall sit in Ashdod, where the fire generates which the Lord sent upon the earth and desires to be kindled. For he baptizes in the Holy Spirit and fire, where there is the cousin and the paternal uncle, ἀδελφὶδος καὶ πατράδελφος, whom the bride desires in the Song of Songs; where there is the fire of the breast and of the most bounteous bosom, of which we read in the same Song: He shall abide between my breasts, and in the Apostle: I gave you milk to drink, not solid food. Where according to the LXX we said: And foreigners shall dwell in Ashdod, in the Hebrew is read, the mamzer shall dwell, or shall sit, in Ashdod, for which we have put: And the separator shall sit in Ashdod. Understand the separator to be the Lord, who separates the wheat from the chaff, and the good fish from the bad fish, and distinguishes silver and gold from filth and dross. And when he has done this, he promises the rest also: I will destroy the insolence, or the pride of the Philistines, for whom the LXX translated foreigners. The Philistines are interpreted in our language falling by the cup, because they drank from the cup of Babylon and, being drunk, fell down. These therefore in the time of the calling of the nations and the coming of Christ shall not have pride, but shall follow the humble and meek Jesus.

And he shall take away from their mouth the blood, words of blasphemy, and the abominations, the worship of idols and the eating of things sacrificed to idols, from between their teeth, so that, after these have been taken away, the Philistines themselves, that is, the foreigners, may be left to the Lord, and may be a leader in Judah, that is, among the people that confesses the Lord, so that the former people which was at the head may be turned into the tail, and the last, which was at the tail, may pass to the head; and that Ekron, once barren and for that reason uprooted, may be as Jebus, that is, as Jerusalem. For this city is called by three names, Jebus, Salem and Jerusalem.

And I will surround, he says, my house, that is, the Church, with those who fight as soldiers for me, that is, with those who serve me in various mysteries, and at my command run hither and thither, going and coming back. Or: I will surround my house with the protection of the angels, of whom it is also written in another place: The angel of the Lord shall send round about those who fear him, and shall deliver them, so that there may be no one who goes and returns, that is, who plots ambushes against my people. Nor shall the exactor pass over it any more, of whom Isaiah says: The exactor has ceased, or else ἐξελαύνων, that is, one who leads out of doors, and drags the bound into captivity, for with his eyes, which we can understand as the prophets and all the saints, the Lord saw the calling of the nations and the security of the Church.

And when they drew nigh unto Jerusalem, and were come to Bethphage, unto the mount of Olives, then sent Jesus two disciples,  Saying unto them, Go into the village over against you, and straightway ye shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose them, and bring them unto me.  And if any man say ought unto you, ye shall say, The Lord hath need of them; and straightway he will send them.  All this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying,  Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass. [Zechariah 9:9] And the disciples went, and did as Jesus commanded them,  And brought the ass, and the colt, and put on them their clothes, and they set him thereon.  And a very great multitude spread their garments in the way; others cut down branches from the trees, and strawed them in the way.  And the multitudes that went before, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest.  And when he was come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, Who is this?  And the multitude said, This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee.

On the next day much people that were come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,  Took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.  And Jesus, when he had found a young ass, sat thereon; as it is written,  Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass's colt. [Zechariah 9:9] These things understood not his disciples at the first: but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him, and that they had done these things unto him.  The people therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of his grave, and raised him from the dead, bare record.  For this cause the people also met him, for that they heard that he had done this miracle.  The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.

"And that expression, 'binding his foal to the vine, and the ass's foal to the vine tendril,' was a declaring beforehand both of the works wrought by Him at His first advent, and also of that belief in Him which the nations would repose. For they were like an unharnessed foal, which was not bearing a yoke on its neck, until this Christ came, and sent His disciples to instruct them; and they bore the yoke of His word, and yielded the neck to endure all [hardships], for the sake of the good things promised by Himself, and expected by them. And truly our Lord Jesus Christ, when He intended to go into Jerusalem, requested His disciples to bring Him a certain ass, along with its foal, which was bound in an entrance of a village called Bethphage; and having seated Himself on it, He entered into Jerusalem. And as this was done by Him in the manner in which it was prophesied in precise terms that it would be done by the Christ, and as the fulfilment was recognised, it became a clear proof that He was the Christ. And though all this happened and is proved from Scripture, you are still hard-hearted. Nay, it was prophesied by Zechariah, one of the twelve [prophets], that such would take place, in the following words: 'Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; shout, and declare, daughter of Jerusalem; behold, thy King shall come to thee, righteous, bringing salvation, meek, and lowly, riding on an ass, and the foal of an ass.' Now, that the Spirit of prophecy, as well as the patriarch Jacob, mentioned both an ass and its foal, which would be used by Him; and, further, that He, as I previously said, requested His disciples to bring both beasts; [this fact] was a prediction that you of the synagogue, along with the Gentiles, would believe in Him. For as the unharnessed colt was a symbol of the Gentiles even so the harnessed ass was a symbol of your nation. For you possess the law which was imposed [upon you] by the prophets."

A spiritual disciple of this sort truly receiving the Spirit of God, who was from the beginning, in all the dispensations of God, present with mankind, and announced things future, revealed things present, and narrated things past-[such a man] does indeed "judge all men, but is himself judged by no man." For he judges the Gentiles, "who serve the creature more than the Creator," and with a reprobate mind spend all their labour on vanity. And he also judges the Jews, who do not accept of the word of liberty, nor are willing to go forth free, although they have a Deliverer present [with them]; but they pretend, at a time unsuitable [for such conduct], to serve, [with observances] beyond [those required by] the law, God who stands in need of nothing, and do not recognise the advent of Christ, which He accomplished for the salvation of men, nor are willing to understand that all the prophets announced His two advents: the one, indeed, in which He became a man subject to stripes, and knowing what it is to bear infirmity, and sat upon the foal of an ass, and was a stone rejected by the builders, and was led as a sheep to the slaughter, and by the stretching forth of His hands destroyed Amalek; while He gathered from the ends of the earth into His Father's fold the children who were scattered abroad, and remembered His own dead ones who had formerly fallen asleep, and came down to them that He might deliver them: but the second in which He will come on the clouds, bringing on the day which burns as a furnace, and smiting the earth with the word of His mouth, and slaying the impious with the breath of His lips, and having a fan in His hands, and cleansing His floor, and gathering the wheat indeed into His barn, but burning the chaff with unquenchable fire.

At another time, he speaks of us under the figure of a colt. He means by [the colt] that we are unyoked to evil, unsubdued by wickedness, unaffected, high-spirited only with him our Father. We are colts, not stallions, "who whinny lustfully for their neighbor's wife, beasts of burden unrestrained in their lust." Rather, we are free and newly born, joyous in our faith, holding fast to the course of truth, swift in seeking salvation, spurning and trampling upon worldliness. "Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion. Shout for joy, O daughter of Jerusalem. Behold, your king comes to you, the just and the Savior, and he is poor and riding upon an ass and upon a young colt." He is not satisfied to say "colt"; he adds "young" to emphasize humankind's rejuvenation in Christ and its unending, eternal youth and simplicity. Our divine Tamer trains such young colts as we little ones. Although the passage speaks of a young ass, it too is a colt.

Everywhere the cause of the unbelief of the Jews was this: that they did not understand Jesus as the "Christ of God", because they always gave their mind to the corporeal histories, unwilling to believe anything spiritual in them. For example, we introduce for the sake of illustration what is prophesied and said in Zechariah, that as it were "upon an ass and a colt He would enter into Jerusalem and would destroy the chariots out of Ephraim and the horse out of Jerusalem". If anyone wishes to understand this of Christ according to the history of the letter, it does not fit; for Christ is nowhere expounded to have destroyed out of Ephraim corporeal and perceptible chariots, nor a corporeal horse from a corporeal Jerusalem. But if you see among the heretics the assemblies of falsehood itself coupled together as by a certain yoke and in evil concord among themselves, which the word of truth is wont to destroy, you will see how Christ, the Word of God, destroys the spiritual chariots out of the spiritual Ephraim; for Ephraim is always set as a figure of the heresies, which have separated themselves from the Church of Christ, just as Ephraim from the tribe of Judah. For just as the divine word spiritually "cast into the sea" the horse and rider of the Egyptians, that is, the impious man together with the devil as his rider and yoke-fellow, so also it destroyed the horse from Jerusalem — whoever is subject to the devil as his rider and not to Christ, as are those horses acceptable to Christ, of whom Habakkuk says: "because you will mount upon your horses, and your cavalry is salvation", that is, upon the apostles and the other saints in whom Christ dwells. Therefore we say: "these in chariots" (pointing to Ephraim) "and these on horses" (pointing to the adversaries of Jerusalem), "but we shall be magnified in the name of our God. They are bound and have fallen, but we have risen and are set upright".

So prophesied Zechariah after the Return from Babylon, in the reign of Darius, King of Persia, when Jerusalem was but just arisen from the desolation which it suffered under the Babylonians. And the whole period from Darius the Persian, in whose time Zechariah prophesied, even to Augustus, Emperor of Rome, amounts to the seven and sixty-two weeks of years in Daniel, which are equivalent to 483 years, as I have shewn in my recent investigations. And neither in the time of the Macedonians from Alexander onwards, not even if you include the reign of Augustus, was anything similar to the words of the prophet fulfilled. For when in those days did the Lord, Whom the prophet speaks of as divine, come among men, and many nations know Him, and confess Him to the only God, and take refuge in Him, and be to Him a people? Or when in the times of the Macedonians or Persians did the king who was foretold come, sitting upon an ass and a young colt? When did He come and utterly destroy the royal array of the Jewish nation, here called Ephraim, and of Jerusalem itself, called chariots and horses, and conquer the army of the Jews? For this is what the oracle revealed, saying:

"Behold thy king cometh to thee, righteous and a saviour, himself meek, and sitting upon an ass and a young colt, and he shall utterly destroy the warlike bow."

For so it was prophesied concerning the destruction of the royal glory of the Jewish nation, at the same time, as, on the other hand, the prophecy of peace for the Gentiles was repeated in agreement with those previously quoted, namely, "And abundance of peace shall be from the Gentiles." In place of which Aquila and the other translators render, "And he shall speak peace to the Gentiles," which stands specially and literally fulfilled from the reign of Augustus, since from that date varieties of government ceased, and peace enwrapped most of the nations of the world. And before the Roman days under Persians or Macedonians what King of the Jews was there, who "ruled from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the earth?" And so the other translators have shewn. Therefore Aquila says:

"And he shall speak peace to the Gentiles, and his power shall be from sea to to sea, and from the river to the ends of the world."

With this agrees the passage in the 101st Psalm concerning the Christ that is to be born of the seed of Solomon:

"In his days righteousness shall arise, and abundance of peace, so long as the moon endureth, and he shall rule from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the world."

For these words about the son of Solomon are as exalted as those in the prophet. When, then, this took place and in what way, and in what period, let him that can, inform me.
The Proof of the Gospel, Book 8, Chapter 4

[Passage quoted, Zech. ix. 9, 10]

As Zechariah prophesied thus after the Return from Babylon towards the conclusion of prophecy, there is no record of a Jewish king, such as the prophecy predicts, except our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, in Whom this prediction was fulfilled, when He literally said to His disciples:

"Go ye into the village over against you, and ye shall find an ass tied and a colt with her; loose them and bring them unto me. And if any man say, What do ye? ye shall say to him, The Lord hath need of them. And they went and did as he commanded them."

Such, then, was the prophecy and such the fulfilment. But what was His riding on an ass meant to shew forth but the lowly and humble manner which marked His first Coming? For the second Coming shall be glorious, that of which Daniel speaks unfolding and revealing his vision:

"9. I saw until the thrones were set, and the Ancient of Days did sit. Thousand thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. 13. And, behold, one as a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven. And he came even to the Ancient of Days, 14. and there was given to him rule and honour and a kingdom, and all peoples, tribes, and tongues serve him. His power is an everlasting power, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed."

But the first Coming of His Incarnation and humiliation has this great symbol and sign among others, the prophecy that He should be called meek and gentle, and that He should come sitting upon an ass. For this is a proof of His sharing our humanity. Whereas the glory of His second divine Coming is shewn by His being borne on the clouds of heaven, and His eternal rule over all nations. And it is reasonable to quote them both to the Jews, and to ask them to explain how they can save the credit of the prophecies, if they confine them to a reference to a single Coming of Christ: for if they both refer to Christ, as they agree, they are bound to tell us when we ask them, how it is possible for the same person at the same coming to be borne upon the clouds of heaven, and also to ride on an ass and a young colt: for these two things are very different. And if you collect the many similar prophecies concerning Christ, and compare their differences side by side, you will decide that some of them refer to His first Coming, being fulfilled at His first Epiphany, while others apply to His second Coming in glory.

For He utterly destroyed by His Divine Power the chariots and horses and weapons of war at His first Coming from the material Jerusalem and the people of Ephraim: wherefore from that day to this their kingdom has never existed, nor their ancient powerful military array or warlike power. And all the Jewish people are here well called Ephraim, not Israel or Judah, so as not to bring into dishonour names of more dignity. And you will find that other prophets call the whole people Ephraim, when charging and accusing them of great crimes, as here. For after the return from Babylon, when the former division of the people had ceased, who are more likely to be meant by Ephraim than the actual inhabitants of Jerusalem? And it was their warlike and military power, that had lasted until Roman times, that our Saviour's Coming destroyed with divine secret power, as the prophecy foretold.

The oracle also calls here on the Church of the Gentiles, not simply to rejoice, But to rejoice greatly, in its message of good news, because of the coming of the Word of God to her; and it calls her the daughter of the heavenly Zion and of the former congregation, because all we that are Gentiles, who believe in Christ, are the offspring and children of Christ and His Apostles, as they whose mother is the Jewish synagogue: and that which follows was also fulfilled at our Saviour's Coming. For unexampled peace has filled all nations from the time of His coming: no longer do states war with states as before, nor nations contend with nations, nor is human life as of old in a state of constant disturbance; Athenians do not attack Lacedaemonians, Syrians Phoenicians, Arabians the inhabitants of Palestine, nor the Egyptians their neighbours. All have been united from that time by God's help, and it is true that there has been "abundance of peace" among the nations from that day to this, according to the prophecy. Jesus alone, and the word of Gospel teaching preached by Him, have ruled men from sea to sea, from the east to the setting sun. and from the rivers to the bounds of the earth, as the prophecy foretold.

Aquila's rendering of this is as follows:

"He shall speak peace among the nations, and his power shall be from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the earth."

Compare with this what occurs in the Psalm, inscribed "To Solomon, of the King's Son," that is to say, of Him that will spring from Solomon's seed, of Whom the Psalm says, "And he shall rule from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the world." And the same Psalm refers to the peace here described, when it says, "In his days righteousness shall arise, and abundance of peace." Isaiah, too, agrees with this when he says, "And they shall beat their swords into ploughshares, and their lances into pruning-hooks; nation shall not take up sword against nation, and they shall not learn war any more." You will find Micah in agreement with this, and many other prophets. And if you note, as I said, the dates, you will be able to appreciate that from the time of Augustus, and of the Epiphany of our Saviour that shone forth in his day, during the period of the Roman Empire the old dissensions and varieties of national government have ceased, and thus from that date the peace of the prophecy began. Just as it then began, a day will come when the prophecy will be fulfilled in all its fullness, when, as the apostle says, "the fullness of the Gentiles shall come in."
The Proof of the Gospel, Book 9, Chapter 17

Without Benjamin, the patriarchs went forth; without Paul, the apostles. Neither of them came first, but being summoned by the first, they made greater profit from the arrival of those who came before. There is, he says, grain in Egypt, that is, where there is greater hunger, there is greater plenty. There is much grain in Egypt. Finally, even God the Father says: Out of Egypt I have called my Son. From this seed comes that abundance. For there could not have been a harvest unless the Egyptians had sown the seed beforehand. Therefore, there is grain that no one believed existed before. The patriarchs trade in this grain. And indeed, they brought silver, but the good Joseph gave grain and returned the silver. For Christ is not bought with money, but with grace. Your price is faith. These divine mysteries are bought. However, that unclean donkey carried this grain in the law, but now it is clean in grace.

But how, after not walking openly in Jewry, and retiring into the wilderness, doth He again enter openly? Having quenched their anger by retiring, He cometh to them when they were stilled. Moreover, the multitude which went before and which followed after was sufficient to cast them into an agony; for no sign so much attracted the people as that of Lazarus. And another Evangelist saith, that they strewed their garments under His feet, and that "the whole city was moved"; with so great honor did He enter. And this He did, figuring one prophecy and fulfilling another; and the same act was the beginning of the one and the end of the other. For the, "Rejoice, for thy King cometh unto thee meek," belonged to Him as fulfilling a prophecy, but the sitting upon an ass was the act of one prefiguring a future event, that He was about to have the impure race of the Gentiles subject to Him. ... But what meaneth, "Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion"? Because all their kings had for the most part been an unjust and covetous kind of men, and had given them over to their enemies, and had perverted the people, and made them subject to their foes; "Be of good courage," It saith, "this is not such an one, but meek and gentle"; as is shown by the ass, for He entered not with an army in His train, but having an ass alone.

Moreover, since the prophet Zechariah exhorts Zion and Jerusalem to a similar gladness, and Matthew says that this very prophecy was fulfilled in the first coming of Christ, we are compelled by necessity, or rather led by the very order of truth, to hope for what is said in Zephaniah not as future but as done. For it is written in Zechariah: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem. Behold, your king comes to you, just and a savior, himself humble and mounted upon a beast of burden and a new colt.

Exult greatly, daughter of Zion; shout for joy, daughter of Jerusalem. Behold, your king will come to you, just and a savior, himself poor and riding upon a she-ass, and upon a colt, the foal of a she-ass. And I will destroy the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the bow of war shall be scattered, and he shall speak peace to the nations, and his power shall be from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the earth. LXX: Rejoice exceedingly, daughter of Zion; proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem: Behold, your king will come to you, just and saving, himself meek and riding upon a beast of burden and a new colt; and he will destroy the chariots from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and he will destroy the bows of the fighters and the multitude, and peace from the nations, and he shall rule over the waters as far as the sea, and the rivers, the outlets of the earth. The evangelists write that this prophecy was fulfilled when the Lord entered Jerusalem, sitting upon a she-ass and the foal of a she-ass, and a crowd of children with branches of palms came to meet him, crying: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, hosanna in the highest; and when the Pharisees rebuked him for not checking the shouting children, he answered: Have you not read: Out of the mouth of infants and sucklings you have perfected praise? Zion therefore exults and Jerusalem shouts for joy, one and the same city — for Zion is the citadel of Jerusalem —, because her king comes to her, who was promised by the oracles of all the prophets. Just, and himself the Savior, that is, Jesus, as the angel interpreted it, speaking to the virgin: And he shall be called Jesus, because he himself shall save his people from their sins. Poor also, or, as the LXX translated, meek, he who, though he was rich, became poor for our sakes; and he says in the Gospel: Learn from me, for I am meek and humble of heart. And riding upon a she-ass, a beast of burden, or upon a new colt, that is, upon both peoples, of the circumcision and of the foreskin, of which the former had borne the most heavy yoke of the law; as it is written in the Acts of the Apostles: Neither we nor our fathers were able to bear the heavy yoke of the law. Hence Paul also writes to the Galatians, who wished to be circumcised: Stand fast, and do not be held again by the yoke of slavery. But the new colt, the multitude of the Gentiles, having no bridle of the law, nor guided by anyone, but always dashed down and broken among the precipices and in the abysses of idolatry, learned by the Lord's sitting upon it to walk and to enter upon the right way.

Now this was done that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, who says: Say to the daughter of Zion: Behold, your king comes to you, meek, sitting upon an ass and a colt, the foal of a beast of burden. This is written in the prophet Zechariah, of whom it will be spoken more fully in its own place, if span of life is granted. For now we must touch briefly on this: that according to the letter, in the short stretch of the journey, he did not rest sitting upon both animals. For either he sat on the ass and the colt was without a rider, or, if he made use of the colt for sitting (which is more fitting), the ass was led along free. Therefore, since the history involves either impossibility or unseemliness, we are carried over to higher things, so that this ass, which was a beast of burden and tamed and had drawn the yoke of the law, may be understood as the synagogue, and the foal of the ass, frisky and free, as the people of the Gentiles, upon whom Jesus sat, his two disciples having been sent to them, one to the circumcision and the other to the Gentiles.

"And Jesus, when He had found a young ass, sat thereon." Here the account is briefly given: for how it all happened may be found at full length in the other evangelists. But there is appended to the circumstance itself a testimony from the prophets, to make it evident that He in whom was fulfilled all they read in Scripture, was entirely misunderstood by the evil-minded rulers of the Jews. Jesus, then, "found a young ass, and sat thereon; as it is written, Fear not, daughter of Zion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass's colt." Among that people, then, was the daughter of Zion to be found; for Zion is the same as Jerusalem. Among that very people, I say, reprobate and blind as they were, was the daughter of Zion, to whom it was said, "Fear not, daughter of Zion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass's colt." This daughter of Zion, who was thus divinely addressed, was amongst those sheep that were hearing the Shepherd's voice, and in that multitude which was celebrating the Lord's coming with such religious zeal, and accompanying Him in such warlike array. To her was it said, "Fear not:" acknowledge Him whom thou art now extolling, and give not way to fear when He comes to suffering; for by the shedding of His blood is thy guilt to be blotted out, and thy life restored.
